Accountable obligation owner.value: Corporate Secretary runs the annual board policy-approval cycle for the group and each IAIG legal entity; Board Governance Lead chairs the pre-read; unresolved policy conflicts escalate to the General Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 7 (Corporate Governance) Standards 7.7-7.8 on delegation to senior management and board oversight, ICP 8 (Risk Management and Internal Controls) Standards 8.1 and 8.8, re-read against the current IAIS ICP consolidated text and the ComFrame CF 7/CF 8 elements at each annual cycle; group-wide supervisor's local governance rules layered on top

In-scope processes.value: Annual governance policy cycle: policy inventory refresh → owner redraft → risk and legal challenge → ExCo endorsement → board committee review → board resolution → publication and attestation, covering the board charter, committee terms of reference, delegation of authority matrix, risk appetite statement, risk management policy, internal control policy, fit-and-proper policy, remuneration policy, outsourcing policy and conflicts policy

In-scope systems.value: Board portal holds the meeting packs, resolutions and minutes; the GRC platform holds the policy inventory, ICP 7/8 mapping and owner attestations; approved PDFs publish to the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Group Policy Governance Procedure — policy tiering (board-approved vs management-approved), annual review calendar, redline and change-log standard, challenge gates for the Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel, resolution wording, and the publication/attestation step

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Risk Committee on recommendation of the Corporate Secretary; re-confirmed each year at the first board sitting and out of cycle whenever the IAIS revises ICP 7 or ICP 8 or the group-wide supervisor issues new governance expectations

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every board-approved policy must be re-approved within 12 months of its last board resolution date; owner redlines due 8 weeks before the target board date, committee pack 10 business days before the committee, board pack 7 calendar days before the board sitting; delegation of authority matrix refreshed within 30 days of any executive appointment

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform policy-review workflow fires owner reminders at T-120, T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to the policy's expiry date, plus a weekly overdue report to the Corporate Secretary and a red flag on the board dashboard for any policy inside 30 days of expiry

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Board and committee minutes, signed resolutions, approved policy PDFs with version and effective date, redlines, and the delegation of authority matrix retained 10 years from supersession in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by legal entity and board date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any policy operating past its 12-month approval expiry, any policy in use without a board resolution, and any delegation exercised outside the approved authority matrix is raised as a governance exception with root cause, owner, remediation date and the next board sitting at which it must be cleared

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Board Governance Lead signs off closure of every expired-policy and out-of-authority exception, and confirms the corrected policy or matrix was tabled and minuted at a named board sitting

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All policies on the board-approved policy register for the group and each insurance legal entity during the year, plus every delegation of authority instrument and every board and committee sitting held in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any board-tier policy operating without a board resolution inside 12 months, any approval not evidenced in the minutes, or any authority exercised above the delegated limit is a fail; two or more fails renders the annual policy cycle ineffective and is reported to the Board Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs annually after the last board sitting of the cycle, with a half-year interim check of the policy expiry dashboard so an expiring policy is caught before it lapses

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Chief Audit Executive owns the review; no reviewer may have drafted, endorsed or presented any sampled policy, and the Corporate Secretary's own cycle records are tested rather than self-attested

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual governance policy-cycle workpaper (policy register extract, minute references, redline trace, delegation matrix re-performance, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under Corporate Governance / ICP 7-8

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Policy register with board approval dates and resolution references, the approved policy set, the delegation of authority matrix and extracted board/committee minutes, producible to the group-wide supervisor or a college of supervisors within 10 business days of a governance information request

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary co-ordinates governance information requests with the Regulatory Affairs Manager; General Counsel clears any response that concedes a lapsed approval or an out-of-authority act before it leaves the group

checklist.step: Refresh the board-approved policy register for the cycle
actions: In the GRC platform open Policy Management ▸ Policy Register and filter Approval Tier = 'Board' and Status = 'Active' for the group and every insurance legal entity.
For each row confirm policy name, owning executive, last board resolution date, expiry date (last approval + 12 months), version number and the legal entities it binds.
Ask the General Counsel and the Chief Risk Officer for any new policy created since the last cycle (new outsourcing arrangement, new AI use, new entity) and add it to the register with an owner.
Retire policies whose subject has moved into another document and record the superseding policy id on the retired row.
Export the refreshed register to the cycle folder as policy-register-<cycle year>.xlsx.
checklist.done: the register lists every board-tier policy with owner, version, last resolution date and expiry date, with no blank owner or expiry field.

checklist.step: Map each policy to the ICP 7 and ICP 8 standards it discharges
actions: Open the IAIS ICP consolidated text at ICP 7 Standards 7.7-7.8 and ICP 8 Standards 8.1 and 8.8 and read the current wording rather than last year's extract.
In the GRC platform link each policy register row to the ICP standard(s) it evidences using the Authority Document mapping tab, and add the ComFrame CF 7/CF 8 elements that apply to the IAIG.
Flag any ICP 7/8 standard with no policy mapped to it as a governance gap and hand it to the Chief Risk Officer to assign a drafting owner.
Record the date the ICP text was read and attach the extract to the mapping record as the citation evidence.
checklist.done: every board-tier policy carries an ICP/ComFrame mapping and every ICP 7/8 standard has at least one policy or a logged gap with an owner.

checklist.step: Lock the board and committee calendar slots for each policy
actions: In the board portal open the annual meeting calendar for the board, Risk Committee and Audit Committee and list every sitting date in the cycle.
Allocate each policy to the committee that must recommend it and the board sitting that must resolve it, keeping each policy inside its 12-month expiry.
Back off the dates: owner redline due 8 weeks before the board date, committee pack 10 business days before the committee, board pack 7 calendar days before the sitting.
Publish the policy-by-meeting schedule to policy owners and load the three back-off dates into the GRC review workflow.
Where a policy cannot fit a sitting before expiry, escalate to the Board Governance Lead the same week rather than letting it lapse.
checklist.done: every policy has a named committee sitting, a board sitting and three loaded back-off dates that all fall before its expiry date.

checklist.step: Issue the review pack to each policy owner
actions: Send each owning executive a review pack containing the current approved PDF, the clean Word source, last year's board minute extract and the ICP 7/8 mapping for their policy.
Include the required change-log template columns: clause, old text, new text, reason, ICP or regulatory driver, and risk impact.
State the redline due date (8 weeks before the board sitting) and that a 'no change' outcome still needs a signed statement of currency, not silence.
Attach the year's open audit findings, regulatory correspondence and incident themes touching that policy so the owner drafts against real events.
Track receipt in the GRC review workflow and chase at T-30 to the redline due date.
checklist.done: every owner has an acknowledged review pack with a redline due date and the year's findings attached.

checklist.step: Rebuild the delegation of authority matrix behind ICP 7.7
actions: Pull the current delegation of authority matrix and the HRIS executive appointment report to identify every role change, joiner and leaver since the last approval.
For each authority line record the decision type, monetary or exposure limit, the named delegate role, the sub-delegation permitted, and the reporting route back to the board.
Reconcile the matrix limits to the actual approval limits configured in the ERP, underwriting and claims systems and list any system limit that exceeds the delegated limit.
Update the matrix within 30 days of any executive appointment and mark the affected lines as changed for the board pack.
Hand the reconciliation differences to the Controller and the Chief Underwriting Officer for correction before the board sitting.
checklist.done: the matrix names a current delegate for every authority line and every system limit reconciles to the delegated limit or has an open correction.

checklist.step: Draft the policy redline with a clause-level change log
actions: Work from the approved source document checked out of the document management repository so no shadow copy enters the cycle.
Mark every change with tracked changes and complete one change-log row per clause: clause reference, old text, new text, reason and ICP or local-regulation driver.
Fold in the year's incidents, audit findings and supervisory feedback rather than cosmetic edits, and state explicitly where the board's risk appetite limits changed.
Where nothing changed, write a statement of currency naming the events reviewed and why no amendment was needed, and sign it.
Check the redline back in as a new draft version and route it to risk and legal review.
checklist.done: each policy has a tracked-change redline or a signed statement of currency, plus a clause-level change log with a stated driver per change.

checklist.step: Challenge the redline against risk appetite and the control framework
actions: Read each redline against the board's risk appetite statement and mark any clause that widens a limit, softens an escalation trigger or removes a control.
Confirm the policy still requires senior management to operate within the board's strategy and risk appetite as ICP 7.7-7.8 expects, with a documented reporting line back to the board.
Confirm ICP 8.1 coverage: the policy set as a whole covers risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting and the internal control system.
Return clauses that breach appetite to the policy owner with the required wording, and log the challenge and its resolution on the change log.
Sign the risk-review field on the policy record only when every raised clause is resolved.
checklist.done: every widened limit or removed control is either reversed or explicitly accepted in writing by the Chief Risk Officer on the change log.

checklist.step: Take the legal and regulatory read across every binding jurisdiction
actions: For each legal entity bound by the policy, check the local governance rules of that supervisor against the group wording and note any local rule that is stricter.
Where a local rule is stricter, add a jurisdiction annex to the policy rather than diluting the group standard.
Confirm the resolution wording proposed for the board is legally sufficient to constitute approval and adoption in that entity's jurisdiction.
Record the legal opinion, date and reviewer on the policy record and attach the reviewed redline.
checklist.done: each policy carries a dated legal review naming every binding jurisdiction and any stricter local rule captured in an annex.

checklist.step: Secure executive endorsement before the policy reaches a committee
actions: Table each redline at the executive committee with the change log, the Chief Risk Officer challenge notes and the legal review attached.
Confirm the operating model can actually deliver the policy: named accountable executive, resourcing, systems and the reporting the board will receive.
Record the executive committee decision (endorse / endorse with amendment / return to owner) in the minutes and on the policy record.
Return any policy the executive cannot operate to the owner with the specific clause and the delivery constraint rather than endorsing it.
checklist.done: every policy going to committee carries a dated executive endorsement naming the accountable executive.

checklist.step: Take the policy through its recommending board committee
actions: Publish the committee pack in the board portal 10 business days before the sitting: redline, clean copy, change log, ICP 7/8 mapping, risk and legal reviews.
At the sitting take the owner through the material changes and the risk appetite impact and record the committee's challenge questions verbatim.
Capture the committee resolution: recommend to board / recommend with amendment / defer, and name any amendment clause by clause.
Send deferred policies back to the owner with a named re-submission sitting inside the policy's expiry date.
checklist.done: each policy carries a minuted committee recommendation, with any amendment recorded clause by clause.

checklist.step: Assemble and issue the board pack
actions: Build the board pack in the board portal: policy register status page, each policy's clean copy and change log, the committee recommendation, and the delegation of authority matrix with changed lines highlighted.
Add the draft resolution text naming the policy, its version, its effective date and the entities it binds.
Publish the pack 7 calendar days before the sitting and confirm every director has opened it via the portal read-receipt report.
Hold a pre-read call with the Board Governance Lead for any policy with a contested clause so the sitting is not the first airing.
checklist.done: the pack is published 7 days ahead with a draft resolution per policy and portal read receipts from every director.

checklist.step: Obtain the board resolution and minute the approval precisely
actions: At the sitting record the resolution for each policy: policy name, version number, effective date, entities bound, proposer, seconder and the vote or unanimous consent.
Minute the board's discharge of ICP 7.7-7.8 explicitly — that the board approved the policy, delegated day-to-day operation to named senior management, and set the reporting it will receive.
Minute the approval of the delegation of authority matrix version and the date from which it operates.
Circulate draft minutes within 10 business days, capture director comments, and have the chair sign the final minutes in the board portal.
checklist.done: signed minutes record a policy-by-policy resolution with version, effective date, entities bound and the delegation approved.

checklist.step: Publish the approved policies and open the attestation window
actions: Publish each approved policy as a locked PDF in the document management repository with version, board approval date and effective date on the cover page, and archive the superseded version.
Update the GRC policy register row with the new resolution date, new expiry date (approval + 12 months) and the minute reference.
Launch the attestation campaign to every in-scope employee population defined by the policy owner, with a 30-day completion window.
Send the changed-clause summary to the affected process owners so procedures and system configurations are updated to match.
checklist.done: the approved version is published and locked, the register shows the new expiry and minute reference, and attestation is running with a stated close date.

checklist.step: Re-point the control library and management reporting at the approved wording
actions: For every changed clause, open the linked controls in the GRC control library and update the control objective, frequency and evidence requirement to the approved wording.
Retire controls whose clause was deleted and create controls for new clauses, each with a named control owner and test frequency.
Update the board and committee reporting pack templates so the board receives the reporting the resolution promised under ICP 8.8.
Reconcile the control library count before and after and hand the difference list to the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: every changed clause has an updated, owned control and the board reporting template matches what the resolution committed to.

checklist.step: File the cycle evidence under the governance retention rule
actions: Move the cycle folder — register extract, redlines, change logs, risk and legal reviews, committee and board packs, signed minutes, resolutions, attestation completion report — into the compliance evidence repository under Corporate Governance / ICP 7-8 / <cycle year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-supersession retention label to every board-approved policy version and its minute extract.
Confirm the repository index makes each record searchable by legal entity, policy name, version and board sitting date.
Confirm attestation completion reached the owner's target and hand the non-completers to the HR Business Partner for follow-up.
checklist.done: the full cycle record is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by entity, policy and board date.

testing.step: Build the population of board-tier policies and governance sittings
actions: Extract from the GRC policy register every policy with Approval Tier = 'Board' that was active at any point in the cycle, for the group and each insurance legal entity.
Extract from the board portal every board and committee sitting held in the cycle with its agenda and minute status.
Add policies referenced in local supervisory returns or in the ORSA but absent from the register so a missing policy cannot hide.
Reconcile the register count to the prior-year closing register plus additions minus retirements and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the prior-year register roll-forward and to the board portal meeting list, and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every active policy to a board resolution inside 12 months
actions: Match each population row to a board resolution on policy name + version + entity and read the resolution date from the signed minutes, not from the register field.
Compute months elapsed between consecutive resolution dates and flag any policy that ran more than 12 months without one.
Flag any policy whose register resolution date differs from the signed minutes — the register is not evidence.
List unmatched and lapsed policies as automatic exceptions with the number of days operated past expiry.
testing.done: every active policy traces to a signed board resolution inside 12 months or is listed as an exception with a day count.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of policies and delegations
actions: Take 100% of policies that changed materially in the cycle, plus 100% of policies mapped to ICP 7.7-7.8 and ICP 8.1/8.8.
Take 10 further policies by seeded random selection from the remainder, and 15 delegation of authority lines stratified across underwriting, claims, investment and expenditure limits.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm the sample covers every insurance legal entity at least once.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all materially changed and ICP-mapped policies, and touches every legal entity.

testing.step: Re-perform the ICP 7/8 mapping on the sample
actions: Open the current IAIS ICP text at ICP 7 Standards 7.7-7.8 and ICP 8 Standards 8.1 and 8.8 and read the wording before opening the mapping record.
Form your own view of which standards each sampled policy discharges, then compare to the GRC Authority Document mapping.
Treat 'mapped to the right ICP but the policy text does not actually address the standard' as an exception, not a documentation point.
Capture the ICP text extract and the mapping screen into the workpaper with the read date.
testing.done: each sampled policy has an independent mapping conclusion and a captured ICP source extract.

testing.step: Trace approvals into the signed minutes and the board portal record
actions: In the board portal open the signed minutes of the sitting cited for each sampled policy and locate the resolution text.
Confirm the minutes name the policy, the version approved, the effective date and the entities bound — a generic 'policies approved' line fails.
Confirm the pack was published at least 7 calendar days before the sitting using the portal publication timestamp and the read-receipt report.
Confirm the committee recommendation pre-dates the board resolution and that any committee amendment appears in the approved version.
testing.done: each sampled approval traces to named, versioned resolution wording in signed minutes with a compliant pack publication date.

testing.step: Re-perform the delegation of authority reconciliation
actions: For each sampled authority line, read the approved limit from the board-approved matrix version in force on the test date.
Pull the configured approval limit for the same decision type from the ERP expenditure workflow, the underwriting authority table and the claims settlement authority table.
Recompute whether any transaction in the cycle was approved above the delegated limit by extracting approvals above the matrix threshold and matching to the approver's delegated role.
Confirm every delegate named in the matrix was in post on the approval date using the HRIS appointment report.
Treat any approval above limit, or by a person not holding that delegation, as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled authority line reconciles between matrix, system configuration and actual approvals, or the breach is quantified.

testing.step: Test the substance of the challenge, not just its presence
actions: For each sampled policy read the change log and check every change carries a stated driver and an ICP or local-regulation reference.
Confirm the Chief Risk Officer challenge notes address any clause that widened a limit or removed a control, and that resolution is recorded.
Confirm the legal review names every binding jurisdiction and that stricter local rules landed in an annex rather than being dropped.
Treat a statement of currency with no named events reviewed as an unevidenced review.
testing.done: every sampled change has a driver, a resolved risk challenge and a jurisdiction-complete legal review, or an exception is raised.

testing.step: Recompute expiry dates and test the reminder and gate mechanics
actions: Recompute each sampled policy's expiry as board resolution date + 12 months and compare to the register expiry field.
Pull the GRC workflow notification log and confirm T-120, T-90, T-60 and T-30 reminders actually fired to the named owner.
Check the overdue report reached the Corporate Secretary weekly and that any policy inside 30 days of expiry appeared on the board dashboard.
Where a reminder fired and the policy still lapsed, record the escalation gap as a control design failure, not a diary miss.
testing.done: recomputed expiry dates agree with the register and every reminder and escalation step is evidenced in the workflow log.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception recording the policy or authority line, entity, what failed and the governance impact.

Assign a root cause from the standing set — owner non-response, calendar slot lost, minute wording insufficient, matrix not refreshed after an appointment, system limit not re-pointed — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any lapsed policy or out-of-authority approval, a named board sitting at which the correction must be tabled.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a named board sitting or retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the annual governance test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for lapsed approvals, unevidenced minutes and out-of-authority acts.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 7.7-7.8 and ICP 8.1/8.8 with the evidence references behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, endorsed or presented none of the sampled policies, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any lapsed approvals to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated ICP-referenced conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Group Privacy Officer owns notice content and the trigger inventory; the Data Protection Officer signs the lawful-basis wording and the Digital Channel Manager owns delivery on the customer journeys

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 19 (Conduct of Business) on fair customer treatment and disclosure at point of sale and ICP 19.12 on protection of policyholder information, read with ICP 22 Standard 22.3 risk-based customer due diligence disclosure expectations; local notice statutes layered per entity (EU/UK GDPR Arts 13-14, Gramm-Leach-Bliley initial and annual privacy notices, PIPEDA, LGPD Art 9, APPI, POPIA s18)

In-scope processes.value: Quote and application, policy issue, beneficiary and dependant addition, claim first notification of loss, servicing address/bank change, medical evidence collection, telematics and wearable enrolment, marketing consent capture, producer-sourced applications and third-party data enrichment — every point at which personal data is first collected or a new purpose begins

In-scope systems.value: Notices are triggered from the policy administration system's correspondence engine and the Customer Self-Service Portal, with contact-centre delivery through Genesys Cloud scripts and producer delivery through the Broker & Agent Portal; delivery events land in the notice log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Privacy Notice Delivery Procedure — trigger inventory by journey and jurisdiction, notice variant matrix, layered notice standard (short-form at collection, full notice linked), timing rule per trigger, channel-specific delivery method, and the evidence event that must be written for every delivery

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Data Protection Officer and countersigned by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; re-approved annually and out of cycle whenever a journey changes, a new data source is added or a jurisdiction amends its notice content rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Notice at or before the moment of collection for direct collection; within 30 days of obtaining data from a third party (bureau, medical, telematics vendor) and no later than first communication; refreshed notice before any new purpose begins; GLBA-style annual notice by the entity's stated anniversary where the exception does not apply

Deadline reminders configured.value: Correspondence engine raises a same-day exception queue for any qualifying event with no notice delivery event within its timing rule; the indirect-collection queue ages at 15 and 25 days against the 30-day window; monthly annual-notice population report to the Privacy Officer 60 days before the anniversary

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Per-delivery record — customer id, trigger event, notice variant and version, jurisdiction, channel, timestamp and the rendered document — retained 7 years from policy termination alongside the versioned notice library showing what text was live on any given date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any collection event with no matching notice delivery, any delivery of a superseded notice version, and any new purpose started before a refreshed notice is raised as a privacy exception with affected-customer count, root cause and a re-notification decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: DPO signs off every re-notification campaign, every decision that a missed notice does not require re-notification, and closure of each notice-gap exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All new applications, policy issues, FNOL records, beneficiary additions, third-party data acquisitions and marketing consent captures in the quarter, by legal entity and jurisdiction, drawn from the policy administration, claims and CRM systems

Pass/fail thresholds.value: ≥99% of collection events must have a matching, in-time, correct-version notice delivery; zero tolerance for a new processing purpose started with no refreshed notice and for indirect collection breaching the 30-day window; below 99% or any zero-tolerance hit escalates to the DPO and the Board Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven and continuous; automated matching of collection events to delivery events runs daily with a monthly exception review, and the full sampled test runs quarterly over that quarter's population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the Privacy Office delivery team and must not have authored the notice variants or configured the correspondence triggers being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly privacy notice delivery workpaper (population extract, reconciliation to collection events, sample, rendered notice inspections, timing recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under ICP 19 / Privacy Notices

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Notice version library with effective dates, trigger inventory, per-customer delivery log extract and rendered notice copies, producible to a data protection authority or market conduct examiner within 10 business days of a request

Regulator response path.value: DPO leads responses to data protection authorities; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager leads market conduct examiner requests; Privacy Counsel clears any response conceding a notice failure before it is sent

checklist.step: Inventory every trigger point at which a notice is owed
actions: Walk each customer journey with the Insurance Product Manager, the Claims Director / Manager and the Digital Channel Manager and list every screen, form, call script and inbound file where personal data is first collected.

Separate direct collection (quote, application, portal registration, FNOL) from indirect collection (credit bureau, MIB, medical records, telematics vendor, data enrichment) — the timing rules differ.
For each trigger record: journey, system, screen or form id, data categories collected, purposes, legal entity and jurisdiction.
Add every new purpose that begins mid-relationship (marketing, analytics modelling, telematics scoring) as its own trigger.
Publish the trigger inventory to the Privacy Office register and date it.
checklist.done: the inventory names every direct and indirect collection trigger with system, screen id, data categories, purpose, entity and jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Set the timing rule for each trigger
actions: For direct collection triggers set the rule to 'at or before the moment of collection' and record which screen element carries the short-form notice.
For indirect collection set 'within 30 days of obtaining the data and no later than the first communication with the individual', and record the clock-start event.
For a new purpose set 'before the new processing begins' and name the event that starts the clock.
Where a jurisdiction demands an annual notice, record the anniversary date convention and the exception test that would remove the requirement for that entity.
Record the local citation behind each timing rule on the trigger row with the date the text was read.
checklist.done: every trigger row carries a timing rule, a clock-start event and a dated local citation.

checklist.step: Build and version the notice variant matrix
actions: Build a matrix of notice variants by jurisdiction, entity, line of business and channel, and give each variant a version number and effective date.

Check each variant states: identity and contact of the controller and DPO, purposes and lawful basis, data categories and sources for indirectly collected data, recipients including reinsurers and service providers, cross-border transfer mechanism, retention periods, individual rights and the complaint route to the supervisory authority.
Draft the layered structure — a short-form notice at the collection point linking to the full notice — and confirm the link resolves for each channel.
Check the reading level and language versions required by each jurisdiction and commission translations early.
Store approved variants in the document management repository as locked PDFs and HTML fragments with the version stamped on the face.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction/entity/channel combination maps to one versioned notice variant carrying all required content elements.

checklist.step: Confirm the notice content matches what the business actually does
actions: Pull the data catalogue entries for the systems behind each trigger and list the actual data elements collected and the downstream consumers.
Compare that list to the data categories, purposes and recipient classes stated in the notice variant and flag anything processed but not disclosed.
Confirm each named recipient class covers the real third parties — reinsurers, TPAs, cloud processors, analytics vendors, producers — using the vendor register.
Hand undisclosed processing to the Privacy Officer to either add to the notice or stop, and record the decision.
Re-run this comparison whenever the catalogue shows a new consumer of the source system.
checklist.done: no data category, purpose or recipient class exists in the catalogue that is absent from the corresponding notice variant.

checklist.step: Configure notice delivery in the policy administration correspondence engine
actions: In the policy administration system open the correspondence configuration and create a delivery rule per trigger keyed on the event code, entity and jurisdiction.
Bind each rule to the correct notice variant id and version, and set the delivery channel by customer contact preference with a paper fallback.
Configure the rule to write a delivery event record — customer id, trigger event id, variant, version, channel, timestamp, render reference — on every send.
Set the rule so a superseded variant cannot be selected once its successor's effective date passes.
Test each rule in the non-production environment with one case per jurisdiction before promoting.
checklist.done: each trigger fires the correct variant and version, writes a delivery event record, and cannot select a superseded version.

checklist.step: Wire the digital and portal collection points to the short-form notice
actions: On every quote, application, registration and claim-report form in the portal, place the short-form notice above the submit control, not behind a footer link.
Confirm the full-notice link opens the current version and that the version id is captured in the page event sent to the delivery log.
Record for each form the notice presentation event — page id, variant, version, session id, timestamp — even where the customer abandons before submit.
Run the forms on mobile viewports and with a screen reader to confirm the notice is presented, not truncated or collapsed by default.
Repeat for aggregator and embedded journeys and confirm the partner presents the same variant.
checklist.done: every portal and partner collection form presents the current short-form notice before submit and logs a presentation event.

checklist.step: Script notice delivery for contact-centre and producer-sourced collection
actions: Add the mandatory notice paragraph to the Genesys agent scripts for new business, FNOL and beneficiary-change call flows, positioned before data capture.
Configure the script step to write a disposition code that generates the notice delivery event and queues the written follow-up notice.
Brief the Broker Relationship Manager to require producers to present the same variant at application and to return the acknowledgement with the submission.
Reject producer-sourced applications with no notice acknowledgement back to the producer rather than issuing the policy without one.
Sample five recorded calls a week against the script step and feed misses to the Contact Center Supervisor.
checklist.done: call scripts and producer submission rules both force notice presentation, and each produces a logged delivery or acknowledgement record.

checklist.step: Run the indirect-collection notice queue against the 30-day clock
actions: Take the daily feed of third-party data acquisitions — bureau pulls, MIB, medical records, telematics enrolments, enrichment files — with the acquisition timestamp per individual.
Match each acquisition to an existing customer notice delivery; where none exists, open a notice case with a due date of acquisition date + 30 days.
Work the queue oldest first and confirm the notice states the source of the data and the categories obtained, as indirect-collection notices must.
Escalate any case reaching day 25 to the Privacy Officer with the individual count and the reason for delay.
Close each case only on a written delivery event, not on a send request.
checklist.done: every indirect acquisition has a notice delivered inside 30 days or an escalated case with a stated reason.

checklist.step: Gate new purposes behind a refreshed notice
actions: Require every product, marketing or analytics initiative that introduces a new purpose to raise a purpose-change request naming the data, the purpose and the population.
Assess whether the existing notice already covers the purpose; where it does not, block the processing until a refreshed notice is delivered to the affected population.
Where the purpose relies on consent, confirm the consent capture and withdrawal mechanism exists before the notice goes out.
Record the block, the notice delivery date and the processing start date on the purpose-change record so the sequence is provable.
Notify the Chief Data Officer to hold the pipeline until the notice date passes.
checklist.done: no new purpose starts before its refreshed notice delivery date, and the sequence is recorded on the purpose-change record.

checklist.step: Publish the current notice to the public and self-service channels
actions: Publish the current full notice per entity and jurisdiction to the public site and the self-service portal with its version and effective date shown on the face.
Keep an accessible archive of superseded versions with the dates each was live so any historical delivery can be evidenced.
Confirm the notice URL used in outbound correspondence resolves to the version live on the send date, not simply to the latest.
Add the notice link to the standard email footer and the portal registration flow.
checklist.done: the current notice and a dated archive of superseded versions are publicly available and version-resolvable per send date.

checklist.step: Reconcile collection events to delivery events daily
actions: Build a daily job in the warehouse that joins qualifying collection events from policy administration, claims and CRM to notice delivery events on customer id and trigger event id.
Apply the trigger's timing rule to classify each match as in-time, late or missing, and compute the delay in days for late rows.
Publish the daily exception file to the Privacy Office with counts by trigger, entity, jurisdiction and channel.
Alert the Privacy Officer the same day on any missing row for a high-risk trigger such as medical evidence or telematics.
Trend the match rate weekly against the 99% threshold.
checklist.done: a daily reconciliation publishes in-time, late and missing counts by trigger and alerts same-day on high-risk misses.

checklist.step: Work the exception queue and decide re-notification
actions: Open a case per exception cluster with the affected individual count, trigger, entity, jurisdiction and the period affected.
Determine root cause — trigger not configured, event code changed, variant superseded, channel failure, producer non-return — from the delivery log and the change record.
Recommend re-notification where individuals were never notified or received a materially wrong variant, and specify the channel and the wording.
Route the recommendation to the DPO for sign-off and execute approved campaigns through the correspondence engine with their own delivery events.
Close the case only when the reconciliation shows the cluster clear on a subsequent run.
checklist.done: every exception cluster has a root cause, a DPO-signed re-notification decision and a clean subsequent reconciliation.

checklist.step: Change-control the notice library
actions: Require every notice text change to enter as a redline with the legal driver, the affected jurisdictions and the proposed effective date.
Review against the current local text and ICP 19 disclosure expectations, then approve the new version number and effective date.
Instruct the Business Systems Analyst to point the correspondence rules at the new version from the effective date and to retire the old version for new sends.
Confirm the archive keeps the superseded version with its live-from and live-to dates.
checklist.done: no notice text changes without a redline, a legal driver, a version number, an effective date and a repointed correspondence rule.

checklist.step: Report notice performance into conduct governance
actions: Assemble a monthly pack: match rate by trigger and jurisdiction, late-delivery days, open exception clusters, re-notification campaigns and complaint volumes citing notices.
Compare the match rate to the 99% threshold and mark every breach with an owner and a recovery date.
Table the pack at the conduct risk forum and escalate any zero-tolerance breach to the Board Risk Committee.
Feed complaint themes about unclear notices back to Privacy Counsel as drafting input.
checklist.done: a monthly conduct pack exists showing match rate against threshold, open clusters, owners and escalations.

checklist.step: Retain the delivery evidence and the version library
actions: Archive the delivery event log and the rendered notice documents into the compliance evidence repository, indexed by customer id, trigger, jurisdiction and send date.
Archive each notice version with its live-from and live-to dates so any historical send can be reconstructed.
Apply the 7-years-from-policy-termination retention label to delivery records and hold the version library for the same period after the last send.
Confirm retrieval by running a spot request for one customer's full notice history end to end.
checklist.done: delivery records and dated notice versions are retained, indexed and provably retrievable for a single named customer.

testing.step: Build the population of collection events for the quarter
actions: Extract every qualifying collection event in the quarter from policy administration (quote, application, issue, beneficiary change), claims (FNOL), CRM (marketing consent) and the third-party acquisition feeds, by entity and jurisdiction.
Add portal and aggregator form submissions and producer-sourced applications so channels outside the core systems cannot be omitted.
Reconcile the extract count to the source-system transaction counts for the quarter and resolve every difference before sampling.
Split the population into direct and indirect collection because the timing rules differ.
testing.done: the population reconciles to source-system counts, is split direct vs indirect, and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile collection events to in-time notice deliveries
actions: Independently join the population to the notice delivery log on customer id and trigger event id, without using the Privacy Office's own reconciliation output.
Apply the documented timing rule per trigger and classify each row in-time, late or missing.
Compute the match rate overall and by trigger, entity, jurisdiction and channel, and compare to the 99% threshold.
List every missing row and every indirect row beyond 30 days as an automatic exception.
testing.done: an independently computed match rate exists by trigger and jurisdiction, with every missing and out-of-window row listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, stratified sample
actions: Take 100% of indirect-collection events and 100% of new-purpose events in the quarter.
Take 40 direct-collection events by seeded random selection, stratified so every jurisdiction, entity and channel in the population appears at least twice.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every high-risk trigger — medical evidence, telematics, minors' data — as a mandatory stratum.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, stratified across jurisdiction, entity and channel, and covers all indirect and high-risk events.

testing.step: Re-perform the variant and version selection for each sampled event
actions: For each sampled event determine independently which notice variant the matrix required, from the entity, jurisdiction, line of business and channel on the record.
Open the correspondence configuration and read the rule that actually fired, then compare the variant and version delivered to your own conclusion.
Check the version delivered was the version live on the send date using the notice version library's live-from and live-to dates.
Treat 'right variant, superseded version' as an exception in its own right.
testing.done: each sampled delivery has an independent variant/version conclusion and a version-currency check against the library.

testing.step: Inspect the rendered notice for the required content elements
actions: Open the actual rendered document or page capture delivered to each sampled individual, not the template.

Tick off controller identity and DPO contact, purposes and lawful basis, data categories, source of indirectly collected data, recipient classes, cross-border transfer mechanism, retention period, individual rights and the supervisory authority complaint route.
Confirm the layered short-form links to the full notice and that the link resolved on the send date.
Mark any missing mandatory element as a content failure regardless of whether delivery was timely.
testing.done: every sampled rendered notice is checked element by element and content failures are recorded separately from timing failures.

testing.step: Trace deliveries to channel evidence and identifiers
actions: For sampled email and portal deliveries, trace the delivery event to the channel transaction id and the bounce/failure status, and treat a hard bounce with no paper fallback as non-delivery.

For sampled call-sourced events, pull the Genesys interaction and confirm the notice script step was performed and dispositioned, listening to the recording where the disposition is the only evidence.
For producer-sourced applications, locate the signed notice acknowledgement returned with the submission in the document repository.
Confirm each traced delivery carries the customer id, trigger event id and timestamp used in the reconciliation.
testing.done: each sampled delivery traces to a channel transaction, recording or acknowledgement carrying matching identifiers.

testing.step: Recompute the timing maths on the sample
actions: For direct events recompute delivery timestamp minus collection timestamp and confirm the notice was presented at or before collection, not after submit.
For indirect events recompute delivery date minus acquisition date and test it against the 30-day window and the first-communication cut-off, whichever fell earlier.
For new purposes recompute notice delivery date against the first processing date in the pipeline log and flag any processing that preceded the notice.
Report the maximum and median delay by trigger so systemic drift is visible.
testing.done: timing is recomputed from raw timestamps for every sampled event with max and median delay reported by trigger.

testing.step: Test the annual-notice and public-publication obligations
actions: For entities owing an annual notice, rebuild the eligible population from the in-force file and confirm a notice was delivered by the stated anniversary.
Where an exception from the annual notice is claimed, read the conditions and confirm the entity's actual sharing practices still satisfy them.
Open the public site and portal and confirm the current notice per entity and jurisdiction is published with its version and effective date visible.
Confirm the superseded-version archive covers the whole quarter with no date gaps.
testing.done: annual-notice populations are covered or a tested exception is documented, and the published archive has no date gaps.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a case per exception with the affected individual count, trigger, entity, jurisdiction and whether the failure was timing, content or non-delivery.
Assign a root cause — trigger not configured, event code drift, superseded variant, channel bounce with no fallback, producer non-return, purpose started early — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and decide re-notification, recording the reasoning where re-notification is not required.
Assess each cluster for local breach-notification obligations and hand qualifying clusters to the incident process.
Carry every open case into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a case, an individual count, a root cause, an owner, a re-notification decision and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the quarterly notice test
actions: Compare the independently computed match rate to the 99% threshold and list every zero-tolerance breach separately.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 19 disclosure expectations and the local notice statutes, citing the workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither drafted the variants nor configured the triggers, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, match rate and open clusters to the conduct risk forum and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, match rate against threshold and forum reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: DPO owns the data-subject rights (DSR) obligation end to end; the Privacy Ops case team performs intake, identity proofing and fulfilment, and Privacy Counsel decides every exemption and refusal

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 19 (Conduct of Business) fair-treatment and information expectations read with ICP 7/8 governance of the models that generate the decisions being contested, and the IAIS Application Paper on the supervision of algorithms and AI in insurance; statutory response clocks taken from each entity's own regime (EU/UK GDPR Art 12(3) one month extendable by two, LGPD Art 19 fifteen days, CCPA/CPRA 45 days extendable by 45, PIPEDA 30 days, POPIA prescribed period), each re-read at the start of every cycle

In-scope processes.value: Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection to processing, withdrawal of consent, opt-out of sale/sharing, and the right to human review of an automated decision — across underwriting decisions, risk scoring, claims triage and fraud scoring where algorithms or advanced analytics drive the outcome

In-scope systems.value: DSR cases run in the workflow/case management tool with fulfilment searches executed against the policy administration system, Guidewire ClaimCenter, the CRM, the enterprise data warehouse and the model governance repository holding the scoring records

Compliance procedure documented.value: Data Subject Rights Procedure — intake channels, identity verification standard by request type, jurisdiction and clock determination, discovery map by system, exemption assessment, model-decision explanation pack, response drafting, redaction standard, and the extension notification rule

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the DPO with Privacy Counsel countersignature; re-approved annually and whenever a new customer-facing system, a new jurisdiction or a new automated decision model enters scope

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per case — clock starts on receipt or, where identity proofing is needed, on receipt of sufficient identity evidence; base SLA taken from the requester's jurisdiction (30 days / one month / 15 days / 45 days) with any permitted extension notified to the requester before the base deadline expires; automated-decision review requests carry an internal 15-day target so the model explanation can be produced in time

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case tool SLA clock fires assignee reminders at 50%, 75% and 90% of the statutory window, a daily breach-risk report to the Privacy Ops lead inside the final 5 days, and an automatic DPO escalation on any case crossing its deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Full case file — original request, identity evidence, jurisdiction and clock determination, discovery results per system, exemption memo, model explanation pack, response letter, disclosure package manifest and delivery proof — retained 6 years from case closure in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every case closed after its statutory deadline, every request refused without a cited exemption, every system omitted from discovery and every automated-decision review answered without a model explanation is logged as a privacy exception with days-late, root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Privacy Counsel signs off every refusal, every exemption applied, every partial disclosure and the closure of each late-case exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All DSR cases opened or closed in the quarter across every intake channel — web form, DPO mailbox, contact centre, producer, regulator referral and postal — for every legal entity and jurisdiction, plus all automated-decision review requests

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of cases closed within the applicable statutory window (extensions count only where notified before the base deadline); zero refusals without a cited exemption and Privacy Counsel sign-off; zero automated-decision reviews closed without a documented human re-decision; any breach escalates to the DPO and, where the regime requires, to the supervisory authority

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per request; SLA monitoring is daily, the exception review is monthly, and the full sampled re-performance test runs quarterly over that quarter's closed cases

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in Privacy Ops and must not have handled, approved or fulfilled any sampled case

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly DSR test workpaper (case population extract, intake-channel reconciliation, sample, discovery re-performance, SLA recomputation, exemption review, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under ICP 19 / Data Subject Rights

Regulator-ready documentation.value: DSR register export with per-case clock dates and outcomes, the case file for any named individual, the discovery system map and the model explanation packs, producible to a data protection authority within 10 business days of a complaint referral

Regulator response path.value: DPO responds to supervisory authority complaint referrals with Privacy Counsel clearing the response; complaints alleging unfair automated decisions are copied to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and the Model Risk Manager

checklist.step: Capture the request and open a case on the day it arrives
actions: Sweep every intake channel daily — the privacy web form, the DPO mailbox, contact-centre disposition codes, producer submissions, postal scans and regulator referrals — and open a case for each request the same day.
Record on the case: requester name, date and time received, channel, the right(s) asserted, the entity and product relationship, and the requester's country of residence.
Classify the right asserted from the wording, not the requester's label — 'send me my file' is access, 'stop using my telematics score' is objection plus possible automated-decision review.
Attach the original request verbatim so the scope cannot drift later.
Acknowledge receipt to the requester within 2 business days stating the right(s) understood and what identity evidence is needed.
checklist.done: every incoming request has a same-day case with channel, rights asserted, entity, jurisdiction and the verbatim request attached.

checklist.step: Verify identity proportionately and start the clock correctly
actions: Apply the identity standard for the request type: authenticated portal session for low-risk access, two matching data points plus a government ID image for erasure and for medical or claims data, and a signed authority plus proof of relationship for agents, attorneys-in-fact and executors.
Do not ask for more data than needed to identify the requester and record why each item was requested.
Set the clock-start date to receipt where identity was already sufficient, or to the date sufficient identity evidence arrived, and write which rule applied on the case.
Where identity cannot be established after two documented attempts, refuse on identity grounds with Privacy Counsel sign-off and tell the requester what would satisfy the standard.
Store identity evidence in the restricted case folder with access limited to the Privacy Ops team.
checklist.done: identity is verified to the standard for the right asserted and the case shows an explicit clock-start date and the rule behind it.

checklist.step: Determine the governing regime and the statutory deadline
actions: Determine the governing regime from the requester's residence, the contracting legal entity and where the processing occurs, and record all three on the case.
Read the current response-period text for that regime and set the base deadline on the case — one month, 15 days, 30 days or 45 days from the clock-start date.
Record whether an extension is available, its length, and that it must be notified to the requester before the base deadline expires with the reason for the delay.
Where more than one regime could apply, apply the shortest deadline and the broadest rights and note the reasoning.
Set the case SLA field so the tool drives reminders from the correct date.
checklist.done: the case names the governing regime with a citation, a base deadline date and the extension rule available.

checklist.step: Run the discovery map across every system holding the requester's data
actions: Open the standing discovery map — the list of systems, owners and search methods maintained against the processing register — and run the search in each: policy administration, claims, billing, CRM, contact-centre recordings, document repository, marketing platform, data warehouse and the model scoring store.
Search on every identifier the requester is known by: policy number, claim number, party id, national identifier, email and phone, because one identifier alone will miss records.
Record per system the searcher, date, identifiers used, hit count and the export location, and record explicit nil returns rather than leaving the row blank.
Ask each system owner to confirm archives, backups and offshore replicas were covered or to state why they are out of scope.
Escalate any system that cannot return results inside 10 business days to the Chief Data Officer.
checklist.done: every system on the discovery map shows a dated search with identifiers used and a hit count or an explicit nil return.

checklist.step: Pull the automated-decision and model records where analytics drove the outcome
actions: Identify from the model inventory every model that scored the requester — underwriting risk score, pricing tier, claims triage, fraud propensity, telematics score — and pull each scoring record with its date, model id and version.
Retrieve the input features used, the score produced and the decision threshold applied, and confirm the version pulled is the one live on the decision date.
Produce the explanation pack: the main factors that drove the outcome in plain language, the data sources behind them, and what a different value would have changed.
Flag any decision made with no human involvement so the human-review right is triggered rather than ignored.
Hand the pack to Privacy Counsel with the model documentation reference for the response.
checklist.done: every model that scored the requester is identified with version, inputs, score, threshold and a plain-language explanation pack.

checklist.step: Assess exemptions and third-party data before anything is disclosed
actions: Review the discovery output for material subject to exemption: legal professional privilege, ongoing SIU or fraud investigation, suspicious activity reporting and tipping-off restrictions, litigation privilege, and third-party personal data.
For each withheld item record the exemption relied on, the citation, the reason it applies to that item, and the date of assessment.
For third-party data decide redact, seek consent or withhold, and document the balancing reasoning rather than blanket-redacting.
Confirm that withholding an AML/CFT report is handled without disclosing its existence, in line with tipping-off restrictions.
Sign the exemption memo and attach it to the case.
checklist.done: every withheld or redacted item carries a named exemption, a citation and dated Privacy Counsel sign-off.

checklist.step: Assemble and quality-check the disclosure package
actions: Compile the package with a manifest listing every document, its source system, date range and page count so the requester can see what was provided.
Apply redactions in flattened form and re-open the output to confirm the redacted text is not recoverable by copy-paste or search.
Include the information the regime requires alongside the data — purposes, recipient categories, retention periods, sources of indirectly obtained data and the rights available.
For portability requests produce a structured, machine-readable export (CSV or JSON) of the data the requester provided, not a PDF bundle.
Have a second Privacy Ops reviewer check the manifest against the discovery log before release.
checklist.done: the package matches the discovery log item for item, redactions are unrecoverable, and a second reviewer has signed the manifest.

checklist.step: Execute rectification, erasure and restriction across every system
actions: For rectification, correct the record in the master system first and confirm the correction propagated to downstream consumers listed in the data catalogue.

For erasure, assess and record what must be retained under insurance, tax, AML and litigation-hold rules, erase the remainder and place the retained set under suppression so it cannot be used for the objected purpose.
For restriction, set the processing-restriction flag in each system and confirm marketing, analytics and model-training pipelines exclude the record on the next run.
Notify recipients the data was disclosed to — reinsurers, TPAs, bureaux, service providers — of the rectification or erasure where the regime requires, and log each notification.
Capture a post-action screenshot or query output per system as proof the change took effect.
checklist.done: the change is applied and evidenced in every system, retained data is justified and suppressed, and downstream recipients are notified.

checklist.step: Deliver the human review for automated-decision requests
actions: Take the model explanation pack and the original file and re-decide the case on its merits without deferring to the score.
Record the reviewer, date, the evidence considered, the conclusion and whether the original outcome stands, is amended or is reversed.
Where the review reverses the outcome, instruct the correcting transaction — reprice, reinstate, reopen the claim — and record the customer remedy.
Where a pattern of reversals appears for one model, raise it to the Model Risk Manager as a potential bias or drift issue with the affected population.
Return the outcome to Privacy Ops for inclusion in the response letter.
checklist.done: a named human reviewer has re-decided the case on the file, recorded the reasoning, and any reversal has a booked correction.

checklist.step: Draft and release the response before the statutory deadline
actions: Draft the response from the approved template covering: rights addressed, action taken per right, exemptions applied with reasons, the model explanation in plain language where relevant, and the route to complain to the supervisory authority.
Have Privacy Counsel clear any refusal, partial disclosure or exemption before release.
Deliver by a channel that produces proof — portal secure message with read receipt, tracked post, or password-protected email with a separately transmitted passphrase.
Record the delivery timestamp and proof reference on the case and close the case only on evidenced delivery.
Where an extension is being used, send the extension notice with its reason before the base deadline, not after.
checklist.done: a cleared response is delivered with proof before the base deadline, or an extension notice was evidenced as sent before it.

checklist.step: Handle refusals and vexatious or excessive claims properly
actions: Where a request is refused, state the specific ground — identity unestablished, manifestly unfounded, excessive repetition, exemption — with the citation and the facts relied on.
For repeat requests record the interval since the previous fulfilment and what changed, rather than refusing on volume alone.
Where a fee is charged for a manifestly excessive request, record the calculation basis permitted by the regime.
Always tell the requester how to complain to the supervisory authority and to seek judicial remedy.
Log every refusal on the DSR register with the ground and the sign-off date.
checklist.done: every refusal carries a specific ground, supporting facts, a citation, complaint routing and a logged Privacy Counsel sign-off.

checklist.step: Run the daily SLA control and escalate breach risk
actions: Open the case tool SLA dashboard daily and review every case at 50%, 75% and 90% of its statutory window with its assignee.
For cases inside the final 5 days, get a written completion plan from the assignee or move the case to a second handler.
Decide extensions before day 20 of a one-month clock so the notice can go out inside the base window.
Escalate any case that crosses its deadline to the DPO the same day with the days-late count and the cause.
Publish the weekly on-time percentage against the 100% threshold to the Privacy Office.
checklist.done: no case reaches its deadline without either completion, a notified extension or a same-day DPO escalation.

checklist.step: Feed request themes back into the privacy control environment
actions: Analyse the quarter's cases by right asserted, entity, product, channel and root cause of the request.
Route repeated rectification requests on the same field to the Data Quality Manager as a data-quality defect with the source system named.
Route repeated objections or automated-decision reviews on one model to the Model Risk Manager and the AI Governance Analyst for a fairness review.
Route requests triggered by unwanted marketing to the Marketing Compliance Analyst with the consent-capture defect identified.
Record each referral with an owner and a due date and track closure at the privacy forum.
checklist.done: each recurring request theme has a named owner outside Privacy Ops, a defect description and a tracked due date.

checklist.step: Maintain the DSR register and the discovery map
actions: Keep one register row per case: case id, entity, jurisdiction, right(s), clock-start, base deadline, extension date, closure date, outcome, exemptions applied, model involvement and days-to-close.
Reconcile the register monthly to the intake channels so a request that arrived by post or through a producer cannot be missing.
Review the discovery map quarterly against the processing register and add any new system, dataset or vendor holding personal data.
Re-test one search method per system each quarter to confirm it still returns records after system changes.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to every intake channel and the discovery map matches the processing register with tested search methods.

checklist.step: Retain the case evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move each closed case file — request, identity evidence, clock determination, discovery log, exemption memo, model explanation, response, manifest and delivery proof — into the compliance evidence repository under Privacy / DSR / <year>.
Apply the 6-years-from-closure retention label and restrict access to the Privacy Office, Legal and Internal Audit.
Purge identity documents at the shorter retention permitted for them once the case is closed and the appeal window has passed, and record the purge.
Confirm retrieval by requesting one closed case end to end and timing the retrieval.
checklist.done: closed case files are filed, access-restricted, labelled for 6-year retention and provably retrievable within the response window.

testing.step: Build the population of DSR cases for the quarter
actions: Extract every DSR case opened or closed in the quarter from the case tool with entity, jurisdiction, right asserted, clock-start, deadline, closure date and outcome.
Independently pull the privacy web-form submissions, the DPO mailbox, contact-centre privacy disposition codes, producer submissions and the regulator referral log for the same period.
Reconcile each channel to the case register and treat any request with no case as an intake failure before sampling.
Add automated-decision review requests as a separate stratum.
testing.done: the case population reconciles to every intake channel with intake failures listed, and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Recompute the clock and test on-time closure across the population
actions: For every case recompute the base deadline as clock-start plus the regime's response period, using the regime the requester's residence and contracting entity actually indicate.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the recorded deadline and flag every case where the recorded date was later than the recomputed one.
Compare closure date to the recomputed deadline and count days-late for each breach, counting an extension only where the notice is evidenced as sent before the base deadline.
Compute the on-time percentage against the 100% threshold overall and by jurisdiction and right.
testing.done: deadlines are recomputed independently and an evidenced on-time percentage with days-late counts exists by jurisdiction and right.

testing.step: Draw a documented, stratified sample of cases
actions: Take 100% of refusals, 100% of automated-decision reviews, 100% of erasure cases and 100% of breached-deadline cases.
Take 25 further cases by seeded random selection across the remaining rights, stratified so every entity and jurisdiction appears.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Include at least two cases arriving through non-digital channels to test intake completeness.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all refusals, erasures, automated-decision reviews and breaches, and spans all entities.

testing.step: Re-perform discovery for each sampled case
actions: Take the requester's identifiers and independently run searches in the policy administration system, claims, billing, CRM, document repository, contact-centre recordings, data warehouse and model scoring store.
Compare your hit counts to the case discovery log system by system and investigate every difference.
Check the discovery map itself against the processing register and flag any system holding personal data that the map omits.
Treat a system searched on only one identifier where several existed as an incomplete search.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent discovery re-performance with differences investigated and map gaps listed.

testing.step: Test identity verification and clock-start integrity
actions: For each sampled case read the identity evidence held and compare it to the standard required for that right and data sensitivity.
Confirm no more identity data was demanded than the standard requires and that the reason for each item is recorded.
Check the clock-start date: where identity was already sufficient at receipt, a later clock-start is an exception that manufactures time.
Confirm identity documents held past their permitted retention were purged and the purge recorded.
testing.done: identity standards and clock-start dates are verified for every sampled case, with manufactured clock-starts listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Review exemptions and redactions on the sample
actions: Read the exemption memo for each withheld item and confirm the cited ground genuinely covers that item on the facts recorded.
Open the released package and confirm redactions are flattened and unrecoverable by copy-paste or text search.
Confirm the manifest matches the discovery log item for item so nothing was quietly dropped between discovery and release.
Treat a blanket redaction with no item-level reasoning, or a refusal with no citation, as a fail rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled exemption and redaction is item-level justified, unrecoverable and reconciled to the discovery log.

testing.step: Re-perform the automated-decision human review
actions: For each sampled automated-decision case, pull the model id and version from the model governance repository and confirm it was the version live on the decision date.
Confirm the explanation pack names the actual driving features and thresholds rather than generic model boilerplate.
Confirm a named human reviewer re-decided the case on the file and recorded reasoning, and that the reviewer was not the model owner.
Where the outcome was reversed, trace the correcting transaction in policy administration or claims and confirm the customer remedy was booked.
Aggregate reversal rates by model and raise any model above the fairness review trigger.
testing.done: each sampled automated decision has a version-correct explanation, an independent human re-decision and a traced correction where reversed.

testing.step: Trace fulfilment actions into the source systems
actions: For sampled rectifications, query the corrected field in the master system and in two downstream consumers to confirm the value propagated.
For sampled erasures, query the erased identifiers and confirm no live record remains outside the documented retention set, and that the retained set carries a suppression flag.
For sampled restrictions, check the record was excluded from the most recent marketing extract and model-training dataset.
Confirm recipient notifications to reinsurers, TPAs and bureaux were sent where required and are logged with dates.
testing.done: every sampled fulfilment is evidenced in the source and downstream systems, with recipient notifications logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an exception per finding with the case id, entity, jurisdiction, right, days-late where applicable and the individual impact.

Assign a root cause — intake channel not swept, identity standard over-applied, system missing from the discovery map, exemption unsupported, extension notified late, human review absent — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and assess whether any breached case must be reported to the supervisory authority or disclosed in the entity's regulatory return.
Where a systemic cause is found, raise a control change with the process owner rather than closing case by case.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, owner, remediation date, a reportability assessment and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the quarterly DSR test
actions: Compare the independently recomputed on-time percentage to the 100% threshold and list every zero-tolerance breach separately.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 19 fair-treatment expectations and the applicable statutory response periods, citing workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled and approved none of the sampled cases, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, breach count and any supervisory-authority-reportable cases to the privacy forum and the Board Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time percentage and reporting date exists in the repository.
