checklist.step: Define the activity inventory from the business, not from systems alone
actions: Run a definition workshop per function — underwriting, pricing, policy administration, billing, claims, SIU, reinsurance, distribution, marketing, financial crime, HR — and list the processing activities each performs.
Set the granularity rule: one activity per purpose, not per system and not per department, so 'fraud detection on claims' is one activity even where four systems serve it.
For each activity name the accountable activity owner by role and the legal entities that perform it, including branches and subsidiaries.
Create the activity shells in the GRC privacy module with owner, function and entity populated before any detail is captured.
Publish the activity list to functional heads for challenge and record their confirmation.
checklist.done: every function has a confirmed activity list at purpose-level granularity with a named owner and the entities that perform it.

checklist.step: Populate the mandatory RoPA fields for each activity
actions: For each activity capture: purposes, data subject categories, personal data categories, special-category data flags, recipient categories, third countries involved, retention period and a description of the technical and organisational security measures.
Capture the controller/joint controller/processor role of each participating entity and the contact details of the controller and the DPO for that entity.
Name the source systems and datasets by their data catalogue ids so the entry can be reconciled rather than described in prose.
Reject entries with free-text placeholders such as 'various' or 'as required' in the retention or recipient fields.
Set the entry status to 'Draft — pending lawful basis' until the basis is determined.
checklist.done: every activity carries all mandatory fields with catalogue-linked systems and no placeholder text in retention or recipient fields.

checklist.step: Determine and document the lawful basis for each purpose
actions: Apply the decision tree per purpose: contract necessity for quote, underwriting, issue, servicing and claims; legal obligation for AML/CFT, sanctions, tax and regulatory reporting; legitimate interests for fraud detection, analytics and direct marketing where permitted; consent only where nothing else applies and it can genuinely be withdrawn.
Never record consent as the basis for processing the customer cannot refuse without losing the contract.
Write the basis and its citation onto the RoPA entry with the date of determination and the counsel who made it.
Where a single activity serves several purposes, split it so each purpose carries its own basis.
Move the entry status to 'Active' only when a basis is present for every purpose.
checklist.done: every purpose within every activity has a named lawful basis, a citation, a determination date and a named determiner.

checklist.step: Record the condition for every special-category and criminal-offence data flow
actions: Identify activities touching health and medical evidence, biometric identifiers, genetic data, criminal convictions from fraud investigations, and any sensitive attributes inferred by models.
Record the specific condition relied on — explicit consent, substantial public interest for insurance purposes, establishment or defence of legal claims, or the local equivalent — with its citation.
Where the regime requires an appropriate policy document alongside the condition, confirm it exists, is current and is referenced on the entry.
Confirm access to the underlying data is restricted to the roles that need it and record the restriction on the entry.
Escalate any special-category flow with no available condition to the DPO to stop the processing.
checklist.done: every special-category and criminal-offence flow carries a named condition, its citation and, where required, a current appropriate policy document.

checklist.step: Complete legitimate-interest assessments where that basis is relied on
actions: For each legitimate-interest purpose write the three-part assessment: the interest pursued, why the processing is necessary and proportionate to it, and the balancing test against the individual's rights and reasonable expectations.
Record the safeguards applied — minimisation, pseudonymisation, opt-out route, retention limit — and the opt-out mechanism the customer actually has.
Re-run the assessment whenever the data sources, the model or the population changes, and date each version.
Route each assessment to Privacy Counsel for sign-off and attach it to the RoPA entry.
Withdraw the basis and stop the processing where the balancing test fails rather than recording a marginal pass.
checklist.done: every legitimate-interest purpose has a dated, signed three-part assessment with named safeguards and an opt-out route.

checklist.step: Record cross-border flows and their transfer mechanisms
actions: List for each activity every country the data reaches, including offshore service centres, cloud regions, reinsurers, TPAs and group affiliates.
Record the mechanism per flow — adequacy decision, standard contractual clauses with their module and execution date, binding corporate rules, or a derogation with the facts relied on.
Attach the executed clauses and the transfer risk assessment for each destination and record the assessment date.
Confirm with the Cloud Architect the actual data residency configuration of each cloud service rather than relying on the contract alone.
Flag any flow with no mechanism to the DPO and suspend the flow until one is in place.
checklist.done: every destination country per activity has a named mechanism, executed documents and a dated transfer risk assessment.

checklist.step: Reconcile the RoPA to the data catalogue every month
actions: Extract from the data catalogue every system and dataset classified as containing personal data, with owner, classification and lineage.
Join the extract to the RoPA on catalogue id and list systems and datasets with no RoPA activity and RoPA entries pointing at retired catalogue ids.
Publish the unmatched list monthly to the activity owners with a 30-day correction window.
Trigger a RoPA change task automatically whenever the catalogue registers a new dataset, a new system or a new personal-data classification.
Report the coverage percentage against the 100% threshold to the DPO monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly reconciliation reports catalogue-to-RoPA coverage against 100% with every unmatched item assigned to an owner.

checklist.step: Reconcile the RoPA to the vendor and model registers
actions: Extract the vendor register for every supplier processing personal data and match each to the recipient categories on the RoPA entries that use them.
List vendors receiving personal data that appear in no RoPA entry and hand them to the activity owner to correct within 30 days.
Extract the model inventory and confirm every model consuming personal data is named on a RoPA entry with its purpose and lawful basis.
Confirm each matched vendor has an executed processing agreement in the contract repository and record the agreement reference on the RoPA entry.
checklist.done: every personal-data vendor and model appears on a RoPA entry with an executed processing agreement referenced.

checklist.step: Set the retention period on each entry and prove it is enforced
actions: Set a specific retention period per data category on each entry — never 'as long as necessary' — derived from the insurance, tax, AML and limitation rules of each binding jurisdiction.
Take the longest applicable period where jurisdictions differ and record which rule drove it.
Obtain from each system owner the configured deletion or archival job and its schedule, and record the job reference on the entry.
Where no deletion job exists, log a control gap with the system owner and a remediation date rather than recording the intended period as achieved.
checklist.done: every data category has a specific retention period, the rule behind it and either an evidenced deletion job or a logged gap.

checklist.step: Record the group-wide AML/CFT record-keeping requirements
actions: Create RoPA entries for customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, sanctions and PEP screening, transaction monitoring, and suspicious activity reporting, each on a legal-obligation basis.

Record the retention floor: customer due diligence and transaction records kept at least 5 years after the end of the relationship or the transaction, extended where a local regime or an open investigation requires.
Confirm the same entries exist for every foreign branch and subsidiary so the group programme applies consistently as ICP 22.6 requires, and list any jurisdiction where local law blocks it.
Reconcile the retention configuration in NICE Actimize and the sanctions screening system to the recorded floor and log any shortfall.
Name the group AML/CFT compliance officer and the local officers on the entries.
checklist.done: AML/CFT activities exist for every branch and subsidiary with a 5-year floor recorded, reconciled to system retention configuration.

checklist.step: Run the annual owner attestation to the 31 March deadline
actions: Launch attestation tasks to every activity owner 60 days before 31 March asking them to confirm purposes, data categories, recipients, third countries, retention and lawful basis are still accurate.
Require a change to be submitted with the attestation where anything moved, rather than a bare confirmation.
Chase at 30 and 10 days and escalate non-responders to their functional head and the DPO.
Freeze and version the attested RoPA on 31 March as the year's record of processing and export it per legal entity.
Log every non-attested activity as an exception with the owner named.
checklist.done: the RoPA is attested, frozen and versioned by 31 March with every non-attestation logged against a named owner.

checklist.step: Gate change so new processing cannot start unrecorded
actions: Add a privacy gate to the change-approval workflow: any change introducing a new dataset, new personal data category, new vendor or new country cannot be approved without a RoPA entry or update reference.
Require the change record to carry the lawful basis for any new purpose and the DPIA reference where the processing is high risk.
Give the Privacy Office reject rights on the gate and record every rejection with the reason.
Sample 10 approved changes a month for gate compliance and feed misses back to the Change Coordinator.
checklist.done: no change introducing new personal data processing is approved without a referenced RoPA entry and lawful basis.

checklist.step: Publish the RoPA views the business and supervisors need
actions: Build the per-legal-entity RoPA export in the format the local regime prescribes and confirm it opens and prints cleanly.
Build management views by function, lawful basis, special-category flag, third country and retention period for the privacy forum.
Publish an internal read-only view so activity owners and Internal Audit can inspect entries without editing rights.
Test the 5-business-day production commitment by running a mock supervisory request for one entity and timing it.
checklist.done: per-entity exports exist in the prescribed format and a timed mock request proves the 5-business-day commitment.

checklist.step: Report RoPA health into privacy and risk governance
actions: Assemble a monthly pack: catalogue coverage percentage, entries missing a lawful basis, special-category entries without a condition, transfers without a mechanism, retention gaps and attestation status.
Mark every zero-tolerance breach with an owner and a recovery date and show the trend against the prior month.
Table the pack at the privacy forum and escalate unresolved breaches to the Board Risk Committee as an ICP 8 internal control matter.
Feed AML/CFT record-keeping gaps to the Financial Crime AML Officer for the group financial crime report.
checklist.done: a monthly pack shows coverage, gaps by category, owners and recovery dates, with breaches escalated.

checklist.step: Retain the RoPA versions and supporting assessments
actions: Archive each frozen annual RoPA version with the attestation signatures into the compliance evidence repository under Privacy / RoPA / <year>.
Archive lawful-basis determinations, legitimate-interest assessments, special-category condition memos, transfer risk assessments and executed clauses alongside the version they support.
Apply the 10-years-from-supersession retention label so the record survives entity restructures.
Confirm the index makes every version searchable by legal entity, activity, lawful basis and third country.
checklist.done: each annual RoPA version and its supporting assessments are archived, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by entity and activity.

testing.step: Build the population from the catalogue, vendor and model registers
actions: Extract from the data catalogue every system and dataset classified as containing personal data, with owner, classification, lineage and legal entity.
Extract the vendor register rows flagged as processing personal data and the model inventory rows consuming personal data.
Extract the frozen 31 March RoPA version for every legal entity, branch and subsidiary.
Reconcile the catalogue extract to the system inventory in the CMDB so a system absent from the catalogue cannot hide the processing behind it.
testing.done: the population covers catalogue, vendor, model and CMDB sources and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every system, dataset, vendor and model to a RoPA entry
actions: Join catalogue ids, vendor ids and model ids to the frozen RoPA and list every unmatched item.
List RoPA entries pointing at retired catalogue ids or terminated vendors as stale entries.
Compute catalogue-to-RoPA coverage against the 100% threshold overall and by legal entity.
Treat every unmatched personal-data system, vendor or model as an automatic exception with the data volume it holds.
testing.done: an independently computed coverage percentage exists by entity with every unmatched and stale item listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, risk-weighted sample of activities
actions: Take 100% of activities flagged special-category, 100% relying on consent or legitimate interests, 100% with a third-country flow and 100% of AML/CFT record-keeping activities.
Take 20 further activities by seeded random selection stratified across function and legal entity, including at least one branch and one subsidiary.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm every function appears at least once in the sample.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all high-risk strata and touches every function, branch and subsidiary.

testing.step: Re-perform the lawful-basis determination on the sample
actions: For each sampled purpose read the current statutory text and reach your own basis conclusion from the facts before opening the recorded basis.
Compare to the RoPA entry and treat 'right basis, wrong purpose split' and 'consent recorded for processing the customer cannot refuse' as exceptions.
Confirm each recorded basis carries a citation, a determination date and a named determiner.
Capture the statutory extract you relied on into the workpaper with the read date.
testing.done: each sampled purpose has an independent basis conclusion and a captured statutory extract.

testing.step: Test special-category conditions and legitimate-interest assessments
actions: For each special-category flow confirm a named condition, its citation and, where required, a current appropriate policy document referenced on the entry.
For each legitimate-interest purpose read the three-part assessment and confirm the balancing test addresses the individual's reasonable expectations and names real safeguards.
Confirm the stated opt-out mechanism actually exists by exercising it in the relevant system or channel.
Treat a template assessment with no activity-specific facts as unevidenced.
testing.done: every special-category condition and legitimate-interest assessment is verified as specific, current and operable.

testing.step: Trace cross-border flows to executed transfer mechanisms
actions: For each sampled third-country flow open the contract repository and locate the executed standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules or adequacy reliance recorded on the entry.
Confirm the clause module and execution date fit the parties' actual roles and that the signature is present, not a draft.
Confirm the transfer risk assessment for that destination is dated and addresses local access laws.
Verify actual data residency with the Cloud Architect for each cloud-hosted flow and flag any residency that contradicts the recorded country list.
testing.done: every sampled cross-border flow traces to an executed mechanism, a dated risk assessment and verified residency.

testing.step: Recompute retention periods and test enforcement
actions: For each sampled activity recompute the required retention from the insurance, tax, AML and limitation rules of the binding jurisdictions and compare to the recorded period.
Pull the configured deletion or archival job for the named system and confirm it runs on the recorded schedule with a job log for the period.
Query the oldest surviving record in the system and compare its age to the recorded period to see whether deletion is actually occurring.
Treat a recorded period with no deletion job or with records surviving past it as a fail.
testing.done: retention periods are recomputed, deletion jobs evidenced by job logs and oldest-record ages tested against the recorded period.

testing.step: Test the AML/CFT record-keeping floor across the group
actions: For each branch and subsidiary confirm customer due diligence, screening, monitoring and suspicious-activity-report activities exist on the RoPA with a legal-obligation basis.

Recompute the retention floor as relationship end date or transaction date plus 5 years, extended where local law or an open investigation requires, and compare to the configured retention in NICE Actimize and the sanctions screening system.
Select 10 closed customer relationships across jurisdictions and confirm the due diligence file and transaction history are still retrievable.
List any jurisdiction where local law prevents applying the group programme and confirm it was reported to the group-wide supervisor as ICP 22.6 expects.
testing.done: the 5-year floor is recomputed and evidenced by retrievable files in every jurisdiction, with blocked jurisdictions reported.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the activity or system, entity, the data volume affected and whether the failure was coverage, basis, condition, transfer or retention.

Assign a root cause — activity never defined, change gate bypassed, catalogue classification missing, vendor onboarded outside the register, deletion job never built, local law conflict — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for unrecorded processing of special-category data or a retention shortfall on AML/CFT records, assess reportability to the relevant supervisor.
Suspend any processing with no available lawful basis rather than scheduling it for remediation.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, owner, remediation date, reportability assessment and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the annual RoPA test
actions: Compare coverage, basis, condition, transfer and retention results to the zero-tolerance thresholds and list each breach separately.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 22 Standard 22.6 and ICP 8.1 with workpaper references behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns and attested none of the sampled activities, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the privacy forum and the Board Risk Committee, copy AML/CFT findings to the group financial crime report, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated ICP-referenced conclusion, coverage percentage and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Intake the arrangement and classify what the vendor will actually do
actions: Open the sourcing request in Coupa / SAP Ariba and require the business owner to state the service, the data the vendor will receive, the countries it will be processed in and whether an insurance function is being outsourced.
Classify the arrangement: processor, joint controller, independent controller, or outsourced regulated function such as claims handling, underwriting authority or customer due diligence.
Reject intake forms that answer the data question with 'none' where the service obviously needs customer records, and send them back to the business owner.
Create the vendor master shell with the classification and the named business owner and route to Third-Party Risk for tiering.
Block purchase order creation until the tiering and contract steps complete.
checklist.done: the request states service, data categories, processing countries and classification, and no purchase order can issue before contracting.

checklist.step: Tier the arrangement on inherent risk and set the clause set
actions: Score inherent risk in the GRC third-party module on data sensitivity, volume, criticality to policyholder service, offshore footprint, sub-processor depth and financial-crime exposure.
Assign tier 1 (material outsourcing or high-volume special-category data), tier 2 or tier 3 and record the scoring evidence rather than the score alone.
Apply the ICP 8.8 materiality test — would failure of this arrangement materially impair the insurer's operations, reputation or ability to meet obligations to policyholders — and record the answer.
Select the mandatory clause set for the tier and data type from the clause library and attach it to the contract request.
Notify the Regulatory Affairs Manager immediately where the arrangement is material so the supervisor notification clock can start.
checklist.done: the arrangement has an evidenced tier, a recorded materiality answer and the mandatory clause set attached to the contract request.

checklist.step: Complete due diligence before any clause is negotiated
actions: Collect the due diligence pack: financial statements, SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate with scope and dates, penetration test summary, business continuity and exit plan, insurance certificates and the sub-processor list.
Run sanctions and adverse-media screening on the vendor entity, its parent and its beneficial owners through the sanctions screening system and file the result.
For offshore delivery, record the delivery locations, staff vetting standard and local data access controls.
Send the security questionnaire to the Security GRC Analyst for review and record their findings and any required remediation as pre-conditions to signature.
Refuse to progress a tier 1 arrangement with an expired certification or an unscoped SOC report.
checklist.done: a dated due diligence pack with in-scope certifications, screening results and security findings exists before negotiation begins.

checklist.step: Draft from the approved clause library and mark the no-edit clauses
actions: Generate the contract in the CLM from the template for the classification so the data-processing schedule attaches automatically.

Confirm the mandatory clauses are present: subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, data categories and data subjects, documented-instructions-only processing, confidentiality of personnel, security measures, sub-processor consent, assistance with data subject rights, breach notification timing, deletion or return at end of contract, audit and inspection rights, and the transfer mechanism.

Add the insurance-specific clauses: regulator access and information rights, record retention aligned to the group schedule, business continuity and exit assistance, and sub-contracting limits on outsourced regulated functions.
Lock the no-edit clauses in the CLM so a negotiator cannot silently weaken breach-notification timing or audit rights.
Record any requested deviation as a clause exception routed to Legal, never as a redline accepted in the document.
checklist.done: the draft carries every mandatory clause from the library with no-edit clauses locked and deviations raised as routed exceptions.

checklist.step: Set the breach-notification and incident clauses to the group standard
actions: Require the vendor to notify the insurer without undue delay and in any case within 24 hours of becoming aware of a personal data breach or a security incident affecting insurer data.

Require the notification to carry the categories and approximate number of individuals and records affected, the likely consequences and the measures taken, so the insurer can meet its own 72-hour regulator clock.
Require co-operation with the insurer's investigation, preservation of forensic evidence and no communication with regulators or individuals about insurer data without written consent.
Name the insurer's 24x7 incident contact route in the clause rather than a generic account manager.
Reject vendor paper offering 'prompt' or 'reasonable' notification with no hour count.
checklist.done: the contract fixes a 24-hour vendor notification with mandated content, evidence preservation and a named insurer contact route.

checklist.step: Fix the AML/CFT and sanctions obligations where the vendor touches customers
actions: For intermediaries, MGAs, TPAs and outsourced screening providers, require them to perform customer due diligence to the group standard and to give the insurer immediate access to CDD records on request.

State expressly that the insurer remains responsible for the AML/CFT obligation regardless of the outsourcing, as ICP 22 expects, and that the vendor must apply the group risk-based approach across customers, products, channels and geographies.

Require notification of any suspicious activity to the insurer's financial crime team, subject to local tipping-off restrictions, and require the vendor to retain CDD and transaction records for at least 5 years after the relationship ends.
Require sanctions screening at onboarding and on every list update, with evidence of list version and screening date available to the insurer.
Include a right to terminate immediately on a financial crime failure.
checklist.done: vendors touching customers carry group-standard CDD, screening, record-retention and reporting obligations with immediate termination rights.

checklist.step: Select and paper the cross-border transfer mechanism
actions: List every country the vendor and its sub-processors will process in, including support and disaster recovery locations, and check each against the exporting entity's adequacy position.

Select the mechanism per destination — adequacy, standard contractual clauses with the correct module for the parties' roles, or binding corporate rules — and execute the documents as a schedule to the contract.
Complete and date a transfer risk assessment for each non-adequate destination covering local government access laws and the supplementary measures applied.
Record the mechanism and assessment references on the RoPA entry for the activity that uses the vendor.
Refuse go-live for any destination with no executed mechanism.
checklist.done: each processing country has an executed mechanism, a dated transfer risk assessment and a RoPA cross-reference.

checklist.step: Control sub-processors by name, not by category
actions: Attach the vendor's named sub-processor list as a schedule with entity name, country, service and data accessed.
Require prior written notice of any addition or replacement with at least 30 days for the insurer to object, and a right to terminate without penalty on unresolved objection.
Require the vendor to flow down the full processing, security, audit and breach clauses to each sub-processor and to remain liable for their acts.
Load the sub-processor list into the vendor register so a fourth party cannot appear unrecorded.
Re-request the list at each annual review and reconcile it to the schedule.
checklist.done: the contract names every sub-processor with a 30-day objection right, flow-down and liability, and the list is loaded to the register.

checklist.step: Secure audit, regulator access and exit rights
actions: Include the insurer's right to audit on reasonable notice, the right to accept a current independent assurance report in place of an on-site audit, and the right to audit on cause without notice after an incident.
Include the supervisor's right of access to the vendor's premises, records and staff for outsourced regulated functions, as ICP 8.8 expects.
Include exit provisions: transition assistance period, data return in an agreed format, certified deletion within a stated period, and continuity of service through the transition.
Include service levels with measurable metrics, reporting frequency and remedies, and name the insurer role that receives the reporting.
Confirm the insurer's exit plan for tier 1 arrangements exists and names the alternative provider or in-house fallback.
checklist.done: audit, supervisor access, exit, data return and certified deletion rights are in the contract and a tier 1 exit plan exists.

checklist.step: Run the clause-completeness gate before signature
actions: Run the CLM clause-completeness check against the mandatory set for the tier and record a pass or a list of missing clauses.
Confirm every deviation carries a written Legal approval naming the risk accepted and any compensating control.
Confirm due diligence, security review and screening results are attached and current at the signature date.
Refuse to release for signature where any mandatory clause is absent without General Counsel sign-off.
Stamp the completeness checklist into the contract record as the evidence of the gate.
checklist.done: no contract reaches signature without a passed clause check or an explicitly signed-off deviation with a compensating control.

checklist.step: Notify the supervisor before a material outsourcing goes live
actions: For each arrangement assessed as material, read the notification requirement of every supervisor with jurisdiction over the contracting entity and record the notice period and format.
Prepare the notification: function outsourced, provider identity and locations, materiality rationale, risk assessment summary, control and audit rights, exit plan and go-live date.
Submit at least the required notice period before go-live, log the submission date and reference, and hold go-live until any objection window closes.
Add the arrangement to the outsourcing register with the notification date and reference.
Re-notify on any material change to the arrangement, provider or location.
checklist.done: every material arrangement has a dated supervisor notification submitted before go-live and an outsourcing register entry.

checklist.step: Execute the contract and open the obligation record
actions: Route the final contract for signature through DocuSign to the authorised signatories per the delegation of authority matrix and confirm both parties signed.
Load the executed PDF, schedules and transfer mechanism documents into the CLM contract record and set the effective, renewal and expiry dates.

Create obligation records for every recurring commitment — assurance report delivery, sub-processor notice, service level reporting, annual certification refresh, audit windows — each with an owner and a due date.
Release the vendor master record for purchase orders and data access only after execution is recorded.
Send the business owner the obligations they must monitor with the reporting cadence.
checklist.done: the executed contract is loaded with dates, obligation records are created with owners, and vendor activation follows execution.

checklist.step: Reconcile active vendors to in-force agreements every month
actions: Extract active suppliers with spend or data access in the month from the procurement system and the accounts payable ledger.
Join to the CLM contract register and list every supplier with personal data access and no in-force processing agreement.
Check the delegated authority register and the reinsurance treaty repository so intermediated and cession data flows are included.
Escalate each unmatched vendor to the business owner with a 15-day deadline to paper or stop the data flow.
Report the coverage percentage to the Third-Party Risk Manager monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly reconciliation lists every data-receiving vendor without an in-force agreement and assigns a 15-day owner deadline.

checklist.step: Re-paper the estate when the clause library changes
actions: On any regime change to mandatory clause content, publish a new clause library version with the effective date and the clauses that changed.
Query the CLM for every in-force contract using the superseded clause and produce the re-papering population by tier and renewal date.
Issue amendment paper to tier 1 vendors within 90 days and fold the change into renewal for lower tiers.
Track re-papering completion weekly and escalate refusals to the General Counsel with the risk and the alternative provider position.
checklist.done: every in-force contract on a superseded clause is identified, with tier 1 amendments issued inside 90 days and completion tracked.

checklist.step: Run the annual vendor review and refresh the evidence
actions: Re-collect the current assurance report, certifications, penetration test summary, continuity test results and sub-processor list for every tier 1 and tier 2 vendor.
Read the assurance report's exceptions and complementary user entity controls and confirm the insurer performs the controls the report assumes it does.
Re-run sanctions and adverse-media screening on the vendor and its owners and re-score inherent and residual risk.
Confirm service level reporting was received at the contracted cadence and log gaps as obligation failures.
Record the review outcome — continue, remediate, exit — with an owner and a date for each remediation.
checklist.done: every tier 1 and 2 vendor has a dated annual review with refreshed assurance, re-screening, re-scoring and a stated outcome.

testing.step: Build the population of third-party arrangements
actions: Extract all active suppliers with spend in the period from procurement and the accounts payable ledger, with entity, category and business owner.
Extract the CLM contract register, the GRC third-party register, the delegated authority register and the reinsurance treaty repository for the same period.
Add vendors identified from the data catalogue and RoPA recipient categories so a data recipient without spend cannot hide.
Reconcile the sources into one population, resolve duplicates by legal entity name and tax id, and flag every source-only row for investigation.
testing.done: a single reconciled population exists across spend, contract, risk, delegated authority and data-recipient sources, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile data-receiving vendors to executed agreements
actions: Identify every population row where the vendor receives personal data or performs an outsourced insurance function.
Match each to an executed contract with a data-processing schedule in force across the whole period the data flowed.
Compare the contract effective date to the first data transfer date evidenced in the interface, file transfer or access logs.
List every vendor with no agreement, a lapsed agreement or a data flow that pre-dates execution as an automatic exception with the data volume involved.
testing.done: every data-receiving vendor traces to an agreement in force before the first data flow, or is listed with the volume exposed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, tier-weighted sample of contracts
actions: Take 100% of tier 1 and material outsourcing arrangements, 100% of arrangements involving special-category data and 100% of vendors performing customer due diligence.
Take 20 further arrangements by seeded random selection across tiers 2 and 3, stratified by legal entity and by offshore versus onshore delivery.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Include at least three contracts executed on vendor paper rather than the group template.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all material and special-category arrangements and includes vendor-paper contracts.

testing.step: Re-perform the clause-completeness check on the sample
actions: Open the executed PDF, not the CLM metadata, and read the contract and its schedules end to end.

Tick off each mandatory clause: documented instructions, confidentiality, security measures, sub-processor consent, DSR assistance, 24-hour breach notification with content, deletion or return, audit and supervisor access, transfer mechanism and record retention.
Confirm every deviation carries a dated General Counsel sign-off naming the risk and the compensating control.
Treat a clause present but materially weakened — 'reasonable' notification, audit only with 90 days notice, unlimited sub-contracting — as a missing clause.
testing.done: each sampled executed contract has an independent clause-by-clause result with weakened clauses treated as missing.

testing.step: Test due diligence currency at the signature date
actions: For each sampled contract compare the dates of the SOC 2 or ISO certificate, penetration test, continuity test and screening result to the signature date.
Confirm the assurance report scope actually covers the service and locations contracted for, not a different product line.
Read the report's exceptions and complementary user entity controls and confirm the insurer-side controls they assume exist and are operating.
Treat due diligence completed after signature as a control failure, not a sequencing point.
testing.done: due diligence is proven current and in-scope at signature for every sampled contract, with post-signature evidence flagged.

testing.step: Verify sub-processors and fourth-party flows
actions: Request the vendor's current sub-processor list directly and compare it to the contract schedule and the vendor register.
Investigate every sub-processor present in reality but absent from the schedule and check whether the 30-day notice right was exercised.
Confirm the flow-down obligations were actually passed on by requesting evidence of the sub-processor agreement for two sampled vendors.
Trace the countries the sub-processors operate in back to the recorded transfer mechanisms.
testing.done: current sub-processor lists reconcile to contract schedules with flow-down evidence obtained and countries traced to mechanisms.

testing.step: Trace transfer mechanisms and residency to executed documents
actions: For each sampled cross-border arrangement open the executed standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules and confirm the module, parties and signature dates.
Confirm the transfer risk assessment for each destination is dated, addresses local access laws and names supplementary measures.
Confirm the actual hosting and support regions configured with the vendor match the countries recorded, using the vendor's configuration evidence.
Flag any live flow to a country with no executed mechanism as a reportable breach rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: each cross-border flow traces to an executed, correctly-moduled mechanism with a dated assessment and verified residency.

testing.step: Recompute materiality and test supervisor notification timing
actions: Re-apply the ICP 8.8 materiality test to each sampled arrangement from the facts — policyholder impact, substitutability, volume, criticality — and compare to the recorded tier.
For arrangements you assess as material, locate the supervisor notification and recompute notification date to go-live date against the supervisor's required notice period.
List arrangements that went live inside the notice period or with no notification at all as reportable breaches.
Confirm the outsourcing register entry matches the contract, the locations and the materiality conclusion.
testing.done: materiality is independently re-assessed, notification lead times recomputed, and understated tiers and late notifications listed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the vendor, entity, service, data volume exposed and the specific clause or control that failed.
Assign a root cause — intake understated the data, tiering wrong, vendor paper accepted, deviation unapproved, sub-processor undisclosed, notification missed, re-papering not run — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where data flowed with no agreement or to an unmechanised country, assess reportability to the data protection authority and the group-wide supervisor.
Suspend the data flow for any vendor with no executed agreement rather than scheduling remediation.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, a reportability assessment and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the annual third-party test
actions: Compare clause completeness, agreement coverage, sub-processor disclosure and notification timeliness to the zero-tolerance thresholds and list each breach.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 8 Standard 8.8 and ICP 22 Standard 22.3, citing workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who negotiated and approved none of the sampled contracts, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unpapered data flows to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated ICP-referenced conclusion, coverage results and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Privacy Officer owns the DPIA programme and the screening gate on every initiative; the DPO signs the residual-risk conclusion and the AI Governance Analyst owns the model-specific assessment sections

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 22 (AML/CFT) Standard 22.3 requiring a documented risk assessment across customers, products, channels and geographies with proportionate enhanced or simplified measures, read with ICP 8 Standards 8.1 and 8.8 on risk assessment within the internal control system and ICP 19 on fair customer outcomes; DPIA triggers and content taken from each entity's regime (EU/UK GDPR Art 35 and the supervisory authority's mandatory-DPIA list, LGPD Art 38, POPIA s55) and re-read at each annual procedure refresh

In-scope processes.value: Every initiative that introduces or materially changes high-risk processing — new products using behavioural or telematics data, underwriting and pricing model deployments, claims triage and fraud scoring, large-scale special-category processing, systematic monitoring, data enrichment and bureau feeds, offshore or cloud migrations of customer data, marketing profiling, and new customer due diligence or transaction monitoring rules

In-scope systems.value: DPIA screening, assessment records and residual-risk decisions live in the GRC privacy module, linked to the delivery record in the PPM tool and to the model entry in the model governance repository; approved DPIAs cross-reference the RoPA entry for the activity

Compliance procedure documented.value: Data Protection Impact Assessment Procedure — mandatory screening questions at initiative intake, the trigger list including the supervisory authority's mandatory categories, assessment content standard, necessity and proportionality test, risk scoring scale, mitigation and residual-risk rules, consultation triggers and the go-live gate

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the DPO with Chief Risk Officer endorsement into the ICP 8 risk framework; re-approved annually and whenever a supervisory authority republishes its mandatory-DPIA list or the group adopts a new class of automated decisioning

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per initiative — screening completed at intake before design work starts; the DPIA completed and signed before any live personal data is processed and before the go-live gate; prior consultation with the supervisory authority lodged where high residual risk remains, allowing the regime's response period (commonly 8 weeks, extendable by 6) before go-live; annual re-review of every DPIA with residual risk above low

Deadline reminders configured.value: PPM tool blocks the design-complete milestone without a screening reference and the go-live milestone without a signed DPIA; GRC raises re-review tasks 30 days before each DPIA's annual anniversary and alerts the Privacy Officer when a linked model version or data source changes

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Screening record, signed DPIA with the necessity and proportionality analysis, risk register, mitigation plan with owners, stakeholder and data-subject consultation notes, DPO opinion, residual-risk decision and any supervisory authority consultation correspondence, retained 10 years from the processing ending

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any initiative live without a completed screening, any high-risk processing live without a signed DPIA, any mitigation past its due date, and any high-residual-risk processing started without the required supervisory consultation is logged as a privacy exception with the population affected, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: DPO signs the residual-risk conclusion on every DPIA, signs off every retrospective DPIA raised after go-live, and approves closure of each unassessed-processing exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All initiatives, projects, model deployments, product launches and material change records that went live in the period, drawn from the PPM tool, the change management system, the model inventory and the product launch register across every legal entity

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of initiatives must carry a completed screening before design-complete; zero high-risk processing live without a signed DPIA pre-dating go-live; zero high-residual-risk processing live without evidenced supervisory consultation; mitigation overdue rate must stay below 10% with no overdue high-severity mitigation; any zero-tolerance hit escalates to the DPO and the Board Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per initiative; the screening-coverage reconciliation runs monthly against the delivery pipeline and the full sampled test runs semi-annually over the initiatives that went live in the half

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the Privacy Office and the delivery function and must not have authored, reviewed or signed any sampled DPIA

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual DPIA programme workpaper (initiative population, screening reconciliation, sample, trigger re-performance, risk-scoring re-performance, mitigation trace, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under ICP 8 / Privacy Impact Assessment

Regulator-ready documentation.value: DPIA register with screening outcomes and residual-risk ratings, signed DPIAs with mitigation status, consultation correspondence and the linked RoPA entries, producible to a data protection authority within 10 business days and to the group-wide supervisor as part of the ICP 8 control evidence

Regulator response path.value: DPO leads prior consultation and any subsequent enquiry from the data protection authority; Privacy Counsel clears every submission; the Chief Risk Officer is informed before any consultation is lodged because it signals unresolved high risk

checklist.step: Screen every initiative at intake
actions: Attach the privacy screening form to the initiative intake in the PPM tool so no initiative can reach design-complete without a screening reference.

Ask the screening questions: new or changed personal data, special-category or criminal-offence data, scale and geography, automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effect, systematic monitoring, vulnerable data subjects, new technology, data matching or enrichment, and offshore or cloud processing.

Score the screening against the trigger list and the supervisory authority's mandatory-DPIA categories, and record the outcome as DPIA required, DPIA not required with reasons, or more information needed.
Where DPIA is not required, record the reasoning in two or three specific sentences about this initiative, never a tick alone.
Publish the screening reference back to the initiative record and notify the delivery lead of the outcome.
checklist.done: every initiative carries a dated screening with a specific reasoned outcome linked to its PPM record.

checklist.step: Open the DPIA and fix its scope
actions: Create the DPIA record in the GRC privacy module linked to the initiative, the RoPA activity and, where relevant, the model inventory entry.
Define scope precisely: the processing operations covered, the systems, the data subject populations, the legal entities and the countries.
Name the assessment team — business owner, delivery lead, data steward, security architect, model owner where applicable — and the deadline, which must pre-date the go-live gate.
State what is expressly out of scope so a later phase cannot be assumed covered.
Book the DPO review slot at the point the DPIA opens rather than at the end.
checklist.done: the DPIA record exists with defined scope, named team, out-of-scope statement, a deadline before go-live and a booked DPO review.

checklist.step: Describe the processing in operational detail
actions: Draw the end-to-end data flow: collection points, systems, interfaces, storage locations, model scoring steps, downstream consumers, third parties and deletion points.
List the data elements by category with volumes and the retention period intended for each.
Record the relationship with the data subject, whether they expect this processing, and how they were or will be informed.
Confirm the flow against the data catalogue lineage rather than the design intent, so the assessment covers what will actually be built.
Attach the flow diagram and element list to the DPIA record.
checklist.done: the DPIA carries a lineage-verified flow diagram, a categorised data element list with volumes and the intended retention per category.

checklist.step: Test necessity and proportionality before assessing risk
actions: State the lawful basis for each purpose and confirm it is recorded consistently with the RoPA entry.
Ask whether the outcome could be achieved with less data, less identifiability, a shorter retention or a narrower population, and record the alternatives considered and why they were rejected.
For special-category or inferred sensitive attributes, confirm a named condition exists and that use in underwriting or pricing is lawful in each jurisdiction.
Confirm data minimisation and pseudonymisation options were tested with the Data Architect, not assumed impossible.
Record a written necessity and proportionality conclusion signed and dated.
checklist.done: the DPIA records tested alternatives, the reason each was rejected, and a signed necessity and proportionality conclusion.

checklist.step: Assess risks to individuals on a defined scale
actions: Identify harms to individuals rather than to the insurer: unfair pricing or declinature, discrimination on protected characteristics, exclusion from cover, loss of confidentiality, identity theft, distress from intrusive monitoring, and inability to contest a decision.
Score each risk for likelihood and severity on the group scale and record the reasoning behind each score in the GRC risk register.
Include security risks from the Security GRC Analyst's threat assessment and continuity risks from the Operational Resilience Analyst.
Rank the risks and mark those that would be high before mitigation, since they drive the consultation test.
Have the business owner acknowledge each risk in writing so ownership is explicit.
checklist.done: every identified harm to individuals carries a scored likelihood and severity with recorded reasoning and business-owner acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Assess algorithmic fairness where models drive the outcome
actions: Pull the model card from the model governance repository: purpose, training data, features, performance metrics, known limitations and version.
Review the feature set for proxies for protected characteristics — postcode, occupation, name-derived features, browsing behaviour — and record the proxy analysis.
Obtain the bias testing results across the relevant subgroups with the metrics and thresholds used, and record disparities that exceed the threshold.
Confirm the explanation method available to a customer contesting the decision and confirm the human review route exists and is resourced.
Record the monitoring plan: drift metrics, fairness metrics, review frequency and the owner who acts on breaches.
checklist.done: the DPIA holds a proxy analysis, subgroup bias results against stated thresholds, a customer explanation route and an owned monitoring plan.

checklist.step: Consult the people affected and the internal specialists
actions: Consult the Chief Info Security Officer's team on security controls, the Operational Resilience Lead on continuity and the Model Risk Manager where a model is in scope, and record each opinion.
Seek data subject views proportionately — customer research, complaint themes, consumer panel or a documented reason why consultation is not appropriate.
Consult the works council or employee representatives where employee data is processed and record the outcome.
Where a processor is central to the design, obtain their input on the security measures they will actually operate.
Attach every consultation record to the DPIA with dates and participants.
checklist.done: security, resilience, model risk and data subject views are each recorded with dates, or a documented reason for omission exists.

checklist.step: Design mitigations with owners and dates
actions: For each risk above the tolerance line define specific mitigations — field-level encryption, pseudonymisation before model training, retention shortening, opt-out route, human review gate, access restriction, monitoring alert — never 'apply controls'.
Name an accountable owner and a due date for each mitigation and mark which must be complete before go-live versus post-go-live.
Re-score each risk after mitigation to give the residual score and record the delta.
Load post-go-live mitigations into the GRC action tracker so they survive project closure.
Refuse to accept a mitigation with no owner or no date.
checklist.done: every above-tolerance risk has a specific mitigation, a named owner, a due date, a pre or post go-live flag and a re-scored residual.

checklist.step: Take the DPO opinion and the residual-risk decision
actions: Read the assessment and give a written opinion on necessity, proportionality, the risk scoring and the sufficiency of the mitigations.
State the residual risk rating and whether it sits below the group tolerance after the pre-go-live mitigations.
Where the residual risk remains high, direct either further mitigation, a scope reduction or prior consultation with the supervisory authority — not acceptance.
Where the business rejects the DPO advice, require the rejection and its rationale to be recorded and escalated to the Chief Risk Officer.
Sign and date the DPIA and set the record status to Approved or Approved subject to conditions with the conditions named.
checklist.done: the DPIA carries a signed DPO opinion, a residual risk rating, and either approval, named conditions, or a direction to consult.

checklist.step: Lodge prior consultation where high residual risk remains
actions: Prepare the consultation submission: processing description, purposes, respective controller responsibilities, measures and safeguards, the DPIA itself, DPO contact and the residual risks driving the consultation.
Lodge it with the lead supervisory authority through its prescribed channel and record the submission date and reference.
Hold go-live for the regime's response period — commonly 8 weeks, extendable by 6 for complex cases — and record the expiry date on the DPIA.
Log every authority question and the response sent, and implement any directed change before go-live.
Inform the Chief Risk Officer and the Board Risk Committee that a consultation is open.
checklist.done: the consultation is lodged with a dated reference, go-live is held for the response period and authority directions are implemented.

checklist.step: Hold the go-live gate until conditions are evidenced
actions: Configure the release approval in the ITSM platform to require the DPIA reference, its status and evidence that every pre-go-live mitigation is complete.
Reject the change where the DPIA is Approved subject to conditions and any condition is unevidenced.
Record who released the gate, on what evidence and when, so the decision is attributable.
For any emergency release without a completed DPIA, require DPO approval, a retrospective DPIA within 10 business days and a logged exception.
checklist.done: no in-scope change is released without a DPIA reference, evidenced pre-go-live mitigations and an attributable gate decision.

checklist.step: Track post-go-live mitigations to closure
actions: Review the GRC action tracker monthly for every open post-go-live mitigation with its owner, due date and evidence status.
Require closure evidence — a configuration screenshot, a policy update, a monitoring alert definition — not an owner's assertion.
Escalate any high-severity mitigation past its due date to the DPO and the business owner's executive the same month.
Compute the overdue rate against the 10% threshold and report it to the privacy forum.
Re-score residual risk where a mitigation is abandoned and re-open the DPO decision.
checklist.done: every post-go-live mitigation is evidenced or escalated, with an overdue rate reported against the 10% threshold.

checklist.step: Re-review DPIAs when the processing or the model changes
actions: Set a re-review trigger on each DPIA for a new data source, a new purpose, a model version change, a new country, a volume step-change or an incident affecting the processing.
Run the annual re-review for every DPIA with residual risk above low, confirming the flow, the mitigations and the fairness metrics still hold.
Where the processing has drifted from the assessed design, open a revised DPIA rather than annotating the old one.
Update the linked RoPA entry with any change in purposes, recipients, countries or retention.
checklist.done: each DPIA above low residual risk is re-reviewed annually or on trigger, with drift handled by a new assessment and the RoPA updated.

checklist.step: Reconcile the DPIA register to the delivery pipeline monthly
actions: Extract every initiative, product launch and model deployment that reached design-complete or go-live in the month from the PPM tool, the change system and the model inventory.
Join to the DPIA register and list every item with no screening reference and every DPIA-required item with no signed DPIA.
Send the unmatched list to the delivery leads with a 10-business-day correction window and copy the Privacy Officer.
Report screening coverage against the 100% threshold to the privacy forum monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly reconciliation reports screening coverage against 100% with every unmatched initiative assigned to a delivery lead.

checklist.step: Retain the DPIA record for the life of the processing
actions: Archive the screening record, signed DPIA, risk register, mitigation evidence, consultation notes, DPO opinion and any supervisory correspondence into the compliance evidence repository under Privacy / DPIA / <year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-processing-ceasing retention label and link the record to the RoPA activity so it is found from either direction.
Keep each superseded DPIA version with its dates so the assessment in force at any past date can be evidenced.
Test retrieval by pulling one DPIA and its full evidence chain end to end.
checklist.done: each DPIA and its evidence chain is archived, version-dated, RoPA-linked and provably retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of initiatives that went live in the half
actions: Extract from the PPM tool every initiative and project that reached go-live in the half, with entity, function and delivery lead.
Extract production change records from the ITSM platform, model deployments from the model inventory and product launches from the product register for the same period.
Add new vendor data feeds and new datasets registered in the data catalogue so processing introduced outside a project cannot hide.
Reconcile the sources into one population and resolve every source-only row before sampling.
testing.done: a single reconciled population of live-in-period initiatives, changes, model deployments and new data feeds exists, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to screening and DPIA records
actions: Match each population row to a screening record and check the screening date pre-dates design-complete.
For every screening that concluded DPIA required, check a signed DPIA exists and its signature date pre-dates go-live.
Compute screening coverage and DPIA-before-go-live rates against the 100% thresholds.
List every unscreened initiative and every late or missing DPIA as an automatic exception with the population of individuals affected.
testing.done: coverage rates are independently computed and every unscreened or late-assessed initiative is listed with its affected population.

testing.step: Draw a documented, risk-weighted sample
actions: Take 100% of initiatives involving automated decisions, special-category data, offshore or cloud migration of customer data, and any consultation with a supervisory authority.
Take 15 further initiatives by seeded random selection across functions and entities, including at least three screened as DPIA not required.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Include every emergency release that bypassed the gate in the period as a mandatory stratum.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all high-risk categories, screened-out initiatives and gate bypasses.

testing.step: Re-perform the screening decision on the sample
actions: Read the initiative's actual design documents and data flows and answer the screening questions yourself before opening the recorded screening.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded outcome, checking the supervisory authority's mandatory-DPIA list as it read on the screening date.
Treat 'DPIA not required' supported only by a tick, or by reasoning that could apply to any initiative, as an unevidenced decision.
Capture the mandatory-list extract and the design document reference into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled screening has an independent re-performed conclusion and a captured mandatory-list extract.

testing.step: Test DPIA content against the required elements
actions: For each sampled DPIA confirm it contains the systematic description of the processing, the purposes and lawful basis, the necessity and proportionality assessment, the risks to individuals and the measures addressing them.
Confirm the flow described matches what was actually built by comparing to the data catalogue lineage and the deployed interface list.
Confirm the DPO opinion is present, dated before go-live, and addresses residual risk rather than merely noting review.
Treat a DPIA describing a design that materially differs from production as void, not as a documentation gap.
testing.done: each sampled DPIA is checked element by element and reconciled to the as-built processing.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk scoring and residual conclusion
actions: Take the identified harms and re-score likelihood and severity on the group scale from the facts recorded, without reading the recorded scores first.
Compare your residual scores to the recorded residuals and investigate every downgrade that has no corresponding mitigation evidence.
Check that any risk you score high after mitigation was either escalated for consultation or further mitigated, not accepted.
Report the count of scores that changed on re-performance as a measure of scoring reliability.
testing.done: risk scores are independently re-performed with unsupported downgrades investigated and a scoring reliability count reported.

testing.step: Test the fairness assessment for model-driven initiatives
actions: For each sampled model-driven initiative pull the model card and confirm the version assessed is the version deployed.
Re-read the proxy analysis and independently check the feature list for proxies the assessment missed.
Re-run or re-read the subgroup bias test results against the stated thresholds and confirm disparities above threshold were mitigated before go-live.
Confirm the customer explanation route and the human review route exist in production by exercising each once.
Confirm the monitoring plan's drift and fairness metrics are actually being produced on the stated cadence.
testing.done: each model-driven DPIA is version-matched, proxy-checked, threshold-tested and its explanation, review and monitoring routes proven live.

testing.step: Trace mitigations to evidence and recompute consultation timing
actions: For each sampled DPIA select all pre-go-live mitigations and trace each to production evidence — configuration, access rule, retention job, monitoring alert — dated before go-live.
For post-go-live mitigations compare due dates to closure evidence dates and compute the overdue rate against the 10% threshold.
For consultations, recompute go-live date minus lodgement date against the regime's response period and flag any go-live inside it.
Confirm every authority direction was implemented and evidenced before go-live.
testing.done: pre-go-live mitigations are evidenced in production, overdue rates computed and consultation waiting periods recomputed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the initiative, entity, individuals affected and whether the failure was screening, assessment, mitigation or consultation.
Assign a root cause — intake bypassed, screening under-answered, DPIA started too late, mitigation unevidenced, design drifted after assessment, gate overridden — and an owner.
Set a remediation date, and where high-risk processing is already live without assessment, decide between a retrospective DPIA inside 10 business days and suspending the processing.
Assess reportability where processing began without a required prior consultation and hand it to Privacy Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next half's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, a suspend-or-retrospect decision and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the semi-annual DPIA test
actions: Compare screening coverage, DPIA-before-go-live rate, mitigation overdue rate and consultation compliance to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 22 Standard 22.3 and ICP 8 Standards 8.1 and 8.8, citing workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and signed none of the sampled DPIAs, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any live unassessed high-risk processing to the privacy forum and the Board Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated ICP-referenced conclusion, coverage rates and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
