checklist.step: Detect and raise the incident with an accurate awareness timestamp
actions: Triage alerts from the SIEM/SOAR, endpoint detection, DLP, the DPO mailbox, the complaints queue and vendor notifications, and raise an incident ticket the moment a signal indicates personal data may be exposed.
Record the awareness timestamp as the date and time of the first signal that gave reasonable indication of a personal data compromise, and write the basis for that timestamp on the ticket.
Never re-date awareness to the point of confirmation — record confirmation as its own field so the clock cannot be quietly restarted.
Set initial severity from the group scale using data sensitivity, volume indicators and system criticality, and page the Incident Response Lead for severity 1 and 2.
Attach the originating alert, log excerpts and detection rule id to the ticket.
checklist.done: an incident ticket exists with a justified awareness timestamp, a separate confirmation field, an initial severity and the originating evidence attached.

checklist.step: Start the notification clock and stand up the response
actions: Start the 72-hour countdown in the ticketing system from the recorded awareness timestamp and confirm escalations are armed at T+12, T+24, T+48 and T+60 hours.
Convene the response bridge with Security Operations, the DPO, Privacy Counsel, the affected system owner, Communications and the Business Continuity Manager.
Assign named owners for containment, forensics, data-impact analysis, notification drafting and customer communications, and set the first checkpoint at T+4 hours.
Open a decision log on the ticket recording every material decision with its time, decider and rationale.
Notify the CISO and the General Counsel immediately for severity 1.
checklist.done: the 72-hour clock runs from the awareness timestamp, workstream owners are named and a time-stamped decision log is open.

checklist.step: Contain and preserve evidence without destroying the record
actions: Isolate affected hosts through the endpoint console, revoke compromised credentials and sessions in the IAM platform, and block the identified indicators at the perimeter.
Capture volatile memory and disk images before remediation and record the hash of each image so the evidence chain holds.
Preserve authentication, database, file transfer and email logs beyond their normal rotation window and record the preservation request and its acknowledgement.
Record the containment timestamp per action, because the regulator submission must state what was done and when.
Confirm with the system owner that containment did not silently destroy the audit trail needed to identify affected records.
checklist.done: containment actions are timestamped, forensic images are hashed and the logs needed for scoping are preserved beyond rotation.

checklist.step: Scope the personal data actually involved
actions: Identify the exact datasets, tables, files or mailboxes exposed and the time window of exposure from the preserved logs.

Extract the affected record set with the personal data categories present — name, contact, national identifier, bank details, health and medical evidence, claims history, beneficiary data — and count distinct individuals, not rows.
Break the counts down by legal entity, data subject country of residence and product, because notification duties follow those splits.
Reconcile the extract to the source-system record counts for the exposure window and record the reconciliation.
Hand the counts and category list to the DPO with the extraction method and the date, and preserve the extract under legal hold.
checklist.done: a reconciled affected-individual count by category, entity and country exists with the extraction method documented and held.

checklist.step: Assess the risk to individuals
actions: Assess the likelihood and severity of harm using the data categories, whether the data was encrypted or pseudonymised and whether the key was also exposed, the volume, the vulnerability of the individuals and whether the data was exfiltrated or merely accessed.
Consider insurance-specific harms explicitly: disclosure of health conditions, claims history, beneficiary relationships, financial hardship indicators and fraud investigation status.
Record whether the data is recoverable, whether it has appeared on a leak site or been offered for sale, and any evidence of misuse.
Write the risk conclusion — no risk, risk, or high risk — with the reasoning, because the two notification duties turn on it.
Reassess as forensics develops and version the conclusion rather than overwriting it.
checklist.done: a dated, versioned written risk conclusion exists naming the harms, the encryption position and any evidence of misuse.

checklist.step: Determine notifiability jurisdiction by jurisdiction
actions: List every jurisdiction implicated by data subject residence, the contracting legal entity, the establishment of the controller and where the data was processed.
For each, read the current notification threshold, window, recipient authority and submission channel, and record the citation and the date read.
Identify the lead supervisory authority where a one-stop mechanism applies, and the insurance supervisors and any cyber authority that must be told in parallel.
Write a notifiability memo per jurisdiction with the conclusion, the threshold applied and the deadline date and time in local time.
Route every not-notifiable conclusion to the DPO for signature rather than closing it in the ticket.
checklist.done: each implicated jurisdiction has a memo with a cited threshold, the recipient authority, a local-time deadline and a signed conclusion.

checklist.step: Draft and lodge the regulator notification inside 72 hours
actions: Draft the submission covering the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate numbers of individuals and records, the DPO contact, the likely consequences and the measures taken or proposed including mitigation.
Where facts are still developing, lodge a phased notification inside the window stating what is known and when the supplement will follow, rather than waiting and missing it.

Have Privacy Counsel clear the wording, then lodge through each authority's prescribed channel — its online breach form, secure portal or prescribed email — and capture the submission receipt and reference number.
Record the submission timestamp per jurisdiction on the ticket against the 72-hour deadline.
Notify the insurance supervisor and, for an IAIG, the group-wide supervisor in parallel where their own rules require it.
checklist.done: every notifiable jurisdiction has a lodged, counsel-cleared submission with a receipt reference and a timestamp inside its window.

checklist.step: Notify affected individuals where the risk is high
actions: Build the notification population from the affected-record extract and resolve current contact details from the CRM and policy administration system, flagging deceased, minor and represented parties for special handling.
Draft the notice in clear language covering what happened, what data was involved, the likely consequences, what the individual should do, the remedy offered and a named contact route.

Choose the channel that reaches the individual — post for financial or health data, email only where the address is verified — and use a public communication where individual contact is disproportionate, with the reasoning recorded.
Stand up the contact-centre response: briefed script, dedicated queue, escalation route and expected volumes, before the first notice lands.
Dispatch without undue delay after the high-risk determination and record the dispatch date, channel, count sent and undeliverable count.
checklist.done: individuals are notified with dated dispatch counts by channel, undeliverables tracked and a briefed contact-centre route live.

checklist.step: Offer and operate the customer remedy
actions: Determine the remedy proportionate to the data exposed — credit and identity monitoring for identifiers and financial data, card reissue, account credential reset, fraud markers on policy and claims records.
Contract the monitoring provider under an executed data-processing agreement before any individual data is shared with them.
Record enrolment counts, the enrolment window and the support route, and monitor take-up weekly.
Track downstream fraud or misuse reports from affected individuals and link them to the incident so the harm assessment stays current.
Report remedy uptake and complaint volumes to the incident forum.
checklist.done: a proportionate remedy is live under a papered agreement, with enrolment, uptake and linked misuse reports tracked.

checklist.step: Handle vendor-originated incidents on the same clock
actions: On receipt of a vendor notification, record the vendor's awareness time, its notification time to the insurer, and the insurer's own awareness timestamp, then start the insurer's 72-hour clock immediately.

Demand the contractually required content — data categories, individual and record counts, consequences and measures — and escalate to the vendor executive sponsor where it is not supplied within 12 hours.
Confirm the insurer, not the vendor, makes the notifiability decision and lodges the notification where the insurer is the controller.
Log any vendor notification received beyond the contractual 24 hours as a contract breach and feed it to the annual vendor review.
Require the vendor's forensic report and remediation plan and verify the remediation before restoring data flows.
checklist.done: the insurer's clock runs from its own awareness, the vendor's late or thin notification is logged, and remediation is verified before restoration.

checklist.step: Send supplementary submissions as the facts settle
actions: Track every commitment made in a phased notification with the date the supplement is due to each authority.
Send supplements with the final counts, root cause, completed containment and the corrective plan, and capture each receipt reference.
Answer every authority question within the deadline stated in its request and log the question and the response sent.
Where the final counts differ materially from those first notified, state the difference and its cause explicitly rather than quietly restating.
checklist.done: every phased notification is followed by a dated supplement with final counts, and every authority question has a logged, in-time response.

checklist.step: Eradicate the cause and confirm recovery
actions: Remove the attacker's persistence, patch or reconfigure the exploited weakness and rotate every credential, key and token in the blast radius.

Validate recovery with the system owner: data integrity checks, reconciliation of transactions processed during the incident window and confirmation that policyholder-facing services are correct, not merely available.
Run a targeted vulnerability scan and a threat hunt across comparable systems for the same indicators before declaring closure.
Record the eradication and recovery timestamps on the ticket for the regulator submission.
Obtain the CISO's written containment and eradication closure before the incident moves to review.
checklist.done: the cause is eradicated, recovery is validated by the system owner and the CISO has signed containment and eradication closure.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review and drive the corrective actions
actions: Hold the review within 15 business days of closure with Security Operations, the DPO, the system owner and the business owner.
Establish the root cause and the control failures, including detection latency measured as first signal to awareness and awareness to containment.
Raise corrective actions in the GRC platform with owners, due dates and severity, covering detection rules, access controls, vendor obligations and the notification process itself.
Feed the incident into the operational risk register and the ORSA scenario set, and update the risk assessment for the affected activity.
Report the review outcome to the Board Risk Committee for severity 1 and 2 incidents.
checklist.done: a review is completed within 15 business days with root cause, measured latencies, owned corrective actions and committee reporting.

checklist.step: Maintain the incident register and the notification evidence
actions: Keep one register row per incident: id, entity, awareness timestamp, confirmation timestamp, severity, data categories, individual counts by country, notifiability conclusion per jurisdiction, submission timestamps and references, individual notification dispatch date and closure date.
Record non-notifiable incidents in the same register with the signed justification, because the regulator can ask why an incident was not notified.
Reconcile the register monthly to the SIEM/SOAR alert queue, the DPO mailbox and the complaints system so an incident cannot exist outside it.
Publish monthly notification timeliness against the 72-hour threshold to the CISO and the DPO.
checklist.done: the register carries every incident including non-notifiable ones with justifications, reconciles to all intake sources, and reports timeliness monthly.

checklist.step: Rehearse the notification path before it is needed
actions: Run at least one annual exercise on a realistic insurance scenario — claims document repository exfiltration or a TPA compromise — with the full response cast.
Time the exercise against the real clock: awareness to scoping, scoping to notifiability decision, decision to lodged submission, and decision to individual dispatch.
Test the mechanics for real: access to the authority portals, current authority contact details, template currency, contact-centre surge capacity and the print or email dispatch route.
Record the lessons as corrective actions with owners and re-test the failed steps within the quarter.
Report exercise results to the Board Risk Committee as ICP 8.8 resilience evidence.
checklist.done: an annual timed exercise proves the portals, templates, contacts and dispatch routes work, with failed steps re-tested inside the quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of incidents for the quarter
actions: Extract every security and privacy incident raised or closed in the quarter from the ticketing system with entity, severity, awareness timestamp and closure date.
Independently pull the SIEM/SOAR alert queue for alerts classified as potential data exposure, the DLP alert log, the DPO mailbox, the complaints system and the vendor notification log.
Match each independent source item to an incident ticket and treat any qualifying signal with no ticket as an intake failure before sampling.
Include incidents closed as non-notifiable, because the notifiability judgement is the substance of the test.
testing.done: the incident population reconciles to every alert and intake source with unticketed signals listed, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Recompute notification clocks across the population
actions: For every notifiable incident recompute the deadline as awareness timestamp plus the jurisdiction's window, in local time, per jurisdiction.
Compare the recorded submission timestamp to the recomputed deadline and count hours late for each breach.
Compute the on-time notification percentage against the 100% threshold overall and by jurisdiction.
Compute detection latency — first alert to awareness timestamp, awareness to containment, awareness to notification — and trend it against the prior quarter.
testing.done: deadlines are independently recomputed by jurisdiction with hours-late counts and latency metrics trended.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of incidents
actions: Take 100% of severity 1 and 2 incidents, 100% of notified incidents, 100% of vendor-originated incidents and 100% of incidents closed as non-notifiable where personal data was involved.
Take 15 further incidents by seeded random selection from the remaining population across entities and data categories.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Include at least three incidents that originated from the complaints queue or the DPO mailbox rather than a technical alert.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all severe, notified, vendor and non-notifiable-with-data incidents.

testing.step: Re-perform the awareness timestamp determination
actions: For each sampled incident read the raw alert, log and mailbox evidence and identify the first signal that gave reasonable indication of a personal data compromise.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded awareness timestamp and quantify any gap in hours.
Treat an awareness timestamp set at confirmation rather than at the first qualifying signal as a clock manipulation exception, because it manufactures notification time.
Capture the originating alert and its timestamp into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled awareness timestamp is independently re-derived from raw evidence with any gap quantified in hours.

testing.step: Re-perform the notifiability determination per jurisdiction
actions: For each sampled incident list the jurisdictions implicated from the affected-record extract's country split, the contracting entity and the processing location.
Read the current threshold text for each and reach your own notifiability conclusion before opening the memo.
Compare to the recorded conclusion and treat a missed jurisdiction as a fail even where the lead authority was notified.
For each non-notifiable conclusion confirm a signed DPO justification exists that engages the actual threshold rather than asserting low risk.
testing.done: each sampled incident has an independent per-jurisdiction notifiability conclusion with missed jurisdictions listed.

testing.step: Trace submissions to authority receipts and reference numbers
actions: For each notified jurisdiction locate the authority's submission receipt or portal confirmation with its reference number and timestamp.
Confirm the submission content covers the nature of the breach, categories and approximate counts, DPO contact, likely consequences and measures taken.
Confirm counts submitted reconcile to the affected-record extract, and where they differ, that a supplement corrected them.
Treat a submission evidenced only by an internal draft or an unacknowledged email as unlodged.
testing.done: each notification traces to an authority receipt with a reference number, and submitted counts reconcile to the record extract.

testing.step: Test individual notification completeness and delivery
actions: Rebuild the notification population from the affected-record extract and compare it to the dispatch count by channel.
Select 25 affected individuals and trace each to a dispatch record with date, channel and address used, checking that verified addresses were used for email.
Read the notice text against the required content — what happened, data involved, likely consequences, what to do, remedy and contact route — in plain language.
Confirm undeliverables were re-attempted through an alternative channel and that the remedy enrolment route worked by testing it once.
Where individuals were not notified, confirm a signed DPO justification engages the high-risk test on the facts.
testing.done: the dispatch population reconciles to the affected extract, sampled individuals trace to dispatch records and the notice content is verified.

testing.step: Test vendor incident handling against the contractual clock
actions: For each vendor-originated incident compare the vendor's own awareness time to the time it notified the insurer against the contractual 24 hours.
Confirm the insurer's clock ran from the insurer's awareness and that the insurer, as controller, made the notifiability decision.
Confirm the vendor supplied the contractually required content and a forensic report, and that remediation was verified before data flows resumed.
Log every late or incomplete vendor notification as a contract breach and confirm it reached the vendor's annual review file.
testing.done: vendor notification timing is measured against the 24-hour clause with breaches logged and remediation verification evidenced.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the incident id, entity, jurisdiction, hours late and the individual count exposed.
Assign a root cause — signal not ticketed, awareness back-dated, scoping too slow, jurisdiction missed, portal access unavailable, template out of date, vendor late — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for an unnotified notifiable incident, instruct immediate late notification with an explanation of the delay rather than silence.
Feed process-level causes into the notification procedure and the next annual exercise scenario.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, a late-notification instruction where needed and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the quarterly notification test
actions: Compare on-time notification percentage, unnotified notifiable incidents and awareness-timestamp integrity to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 8 Standard 8.8 and ICP 19.12, citing workpaper references and the measured detection latencies.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled and notified none of the sampled incidents, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any unnotified incidents and the latency trend to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated ICP-referenced conclusion, timeliness percentage and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Scope the in-scope population from HR and entitlement data
actions: Extract from Workday HCM every active employee, secondee and intern with legal entity, location, function, job profile, manager and start date.
Add the contractor register and offshore service-centre rosters, which sit outside the HCM worker record but hold the same data access.
Join the IAM entitlement extract so anyone with access to policy administration, claims, CRM, the data warehouse or document repositories is captured regardless of job title.
Apply the scoping rule — anyone with access to personal data, anyone who can request it, and every people manager — and record the rationale for anyone excluded.
Publish the population with counts by entity, function and location and have each functional head confirm it.
checklist.done: the population is built from HCM, contractor and IAM sources with a recorded rationale for every exclusion and functional-head confirmation.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum against the year's real events
actions: Review the year's privacy incidents, DSR themes, complaint drivers, audit findings and supervisory feedback and list the behaviours that need to change.

Update the core module: lawful basis in insurance context, data minimisation in underwriting and claims files, handling special-category medical evidence, secure sharing with producers and TPAs, recognising a data subject request in any channel, and incident reporting within the hour.
Update the ICP 22 component with the group AML/CFT record-keeping and customer due diligence expectations that apply to all branches and subsidiaries.
Retire content that no longer reflects the systems or the procedures and record the change log with the driver for each change.
Have Privacy Counsel and the Financial Crime AML Officer review the content for legal and financial crime accuracy before build.
checklist.done: the curriculum change log names the incident, finding or regime change behind every change and carries legal and financial crime review.

checklist.step: Build the role-based modules on top of the core
actions: Build role modules with scenarios from the actual job: claims handlers redacting third-party data in a claim file, contact-centre agents verifying identity before disclosure, underwriters handling medical evidence, marketing staff applying consent and opt-out, analysts handling bulk extracts, and financial crime staff on CDD record-keeping and tipping-off.
Build a manager module covering approving access, handling a team member's data mishandling and escalating an incident.
Set the assessment at a minimum 80% pass mark with scenario questions rather than definition recall, and cap re-sits at three before manager escalation.
Localise language and jurisdiction-specific rules for each region and confirm the offshore centres receive the version that matches their local law.
Pilot each module with a small cohort and fix the questions with anomalous failure rates before release.
checklist.done: each role has a scenario-based module with an 80% pass mark, localised content and a pilot-tested assessment.

checklist.step: Map every person to the modules their role requires
actions: Build LMS assignment rules keyed on job profile, entitlement group and location so the mapping is automatic rather than a manual list.
Assign the core module to the entire population and layer role modules by rule, adding the manager module to everyone with direct reports.
Test the rules against the published population and reconcile assignment counts to population counts before launch.
Handle exceptions explicitly — long-term leave, notice period, no-system-access roles — through a documented deferral with an owner and a return date, never by silent removal.
Confirm contractors and offshore staff have LMS accounts or a tracked equivalent delivery with the same assessment.
checklist.done: assignment counts reconcile to population counts and every deferral is documented with an owner and a return date.

checklist.step: Launch the annual cycle on 1 September
actions: Open the campaign on 1 September with a launch communication from the DPO and the Chief HR Officer stating the 30 November deadline and the consequence of non-completion.
Configure learner reminders at 30, 14, 7 and 2 days to close and weekly manager non-completer reports from 1 November.
Publish a live completion dashboard by entity, function, location and manager visible to functional heads.
Brief the service desk on access issues and monitor course launch failures daily in the first week so technical problems are not mistaken for non-completion.
Track completion velocity weekly against the prior year's curve and intervene where a function lags.
checklist.done: the campaign is live with dated communications, configured reminders, a live dashboard and weekly velocity tracking.

checklist.step: Assign and track onboarding training within 30 days of hire
actions: Trigger the LMS assignment automatically from the Workday hire event so the assignment exists on day one, not after the first HR cycle.
Set the due date at start date + 30 days and alert the line manager at day 20 and day 27.
Run a daily job listing new starters with system access granted and no training assignment, and clear each within 5 days.
Apply the same rule to contractors and offshore staff from their access-grant date rather than a payroll date.
Report joiner completion within 30 days as a monthly metric to the Privacy Officer.
checklist.done: every new starter and contractor has a day-one assignment, a start-plus-30 due date and monthly reported joiner timeliness.

checklist.step: Catch movers into data-handling roles
actions: Monitor the Workday job change and transfer report weekly for moves into functions with personal data access.
Assign the new role module with a due date of transfer effective date + 30 days and notify the receiving manager.
Coordinate with the Access Management Analyst so new entitlements and the training assignment are granted together, not weeks apart.
Remove role modules that no longer apply so completion statistics are not inflated by irrelevant assignments.
Escalate movers with new access and no completion at day 30 to the receiving functional head.
checklist.done: every mover into a data-handling role has a role module assigned within days of transfer and escalation at day 30.

checklist.step: Deliver targeted refreshers after incidents and findings
actions: Take the corrective actions from privacy incidents, DSR failures and audit findings and identify the specific teams whose behaviour must change.
Build a short targeted session using the real anonymised case and the correct handling, and deliver it within 30 days of the post-incident review.
Record attendance against named individuals in the LMS so the refresher counts as evidence, not as an informal briefing.
Re-test the behaviour after 60 days — a spot check of file redaction quality or identity verification on recorded calls — and report the result.
Feed persistent failures back into the next annual curriculum.
checklist.done: each incident-driven refresher is delivered within 30 days, attendance is recorded by name and behaviour is re-tested at 60 days.

checklist.step: Escalate non-completion up a defined ladder
actions: From 1 November send weekly named non-completer lists to line managers with the deadline and the consequence stated.
On 1 December escalate remaining non-completers to their functional head and the HR Business Partner with the data access each person holds.
At 15 days past deadline recommend suspension of access to personal data systems for anyone still outstanding, and execute it with the Access Management Analyst on approval.
Record a performance file entry for persistent non-completion with the Chief HR Officer's sign-off.
Never close the cycle by writing off outstanding learners — each must complete or have an approved, dated deferral.
checklist.done: the escalation ladder is evidenced week by week and every outstanding learner ends with completion, suspension or an approved deferral.

checklist.step: Cover the offshore and outsourced populations
actions: List every offshore service centre and outsourced team handling insurer personal data with headcount by location and the data they access.
Confirm each is either enrolled in the insurer's LMS or delivers an equivalent programme with the insurer's content and assessment.
Obtain quarterly completion evidence per named individual, not an aggregate percentage, and reconcile it to the vendor's headcount.
Apply the same 30-day joiner rule to vendor staff onboarding to insurer systems.
Log shortfalls as contract obligation failures and feed them into the annual vendor review.
checklist.done: every offshore and outsourced population has named-individual completion evidence reconciled to headcount, with shortfalls logged as obligation failures.

checklist.step: Test whether the training changed behaviour
actions: Define behaviour measures rather than completion measures: incidents caused by human error, DSRs missed at first contact, mis-sent correspondence, over-collection in underwriting files and redaction quality in claims files.
Baseline each measure before the cycle and re-measure 90 days after close, by function.
Where a function shows no improvement, redesign its module content rather than repeating the same course.
Run a phishing-style privacy scenario test — an unauthorised request for customer data by phone or email — and record the response rate by function.
Report behaviour outcomes alongside completion at the privacy forum.
checklist.done: behaviour measures are baselined and re-measured 90 days post-cycle by function, with content redesigned where no improvement appears.

checklist.step: Reconcile completion to the population monthly
actions: Each month re-extract the population from HCM, the contractor register and the IAM entitlements and join it to LMS assignments and completions.
List individuals with personal data access and no assignment, assignments with no matching worker record, and completions recorded against leavers.
Compute the completion percentage against the 98% threshold and the 100% sub-thresholds for special-category, financial crime and bulk-export roles.
Publish the reconciliation to the Privacy Officer and the Learning Development Manager with the unmatched lists.
Investigate every unmatched item rather than adjusting the denominator.
checklist.done: a monthly reconciliation reports completion against threshold with unmatched lists investigated and no denominator adjustment.

checklist.step: Certify completion to governance
actions: Assemble the cycle certification by 31 January: population definition and scoping rationale, completion by entity, function and location, sub-threshold results, deferrals, access suspensions and behaviour outcomes.
State plainly where thresholds were missed, by whom and what was done, rather than presenting only the headline percentage.
Table the certification at the Board Risk Committee as ICP 8 competence evidence and copy the AML/CFT component to the Financial Crime AML Officer for the group financial crime report.
Record the committee's direction on any missed threshold with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: a dated certification with population rationale, threshold results and misses is tabled at the Board Risk Committee by 31 January.

checklist.step: Version and archive the course content
actions: Archive each course version with its syllabus, assessment bank, effective dates and the change log for the cycle.
Ensure every completion record stores the course version taken so a completion can be tied to the content in force at the time.
Retire superseded versions from assignment while retaining them for evidence.
Confirm certificates carry learner name, course, version, score and completion timestamp.
checklist.done: each course version is archived with its syllabus and dates, and every completion record names the version taken.

checklist.step: Retain the training evidence for the full retention period
actions: Export the cycle's completion records, population extracts, reconciliations, deferral approvals, escalation correspondence and the certification into the compliance evidence repository under Privacy / Training / <cycle year>.
Apply the 7-years-from-completion retention label and confirm leaver records survive the HCM purge so historical completion can still be evidenced.
Confirm the index makes records searchable by learner, entity, function, course version and completion date.
Test retrieval by producing one named individual's full training history end to end.
checklist.done: cycle evidence is archived, labelled for 7-year retention, survives HCM purges and is provably retrievable per named learner.

testing.step: Build the in-scope learner population independently
actions: Extract all active workers from Workday HCM for the cycle with entity, location, function, job profile, start date and termination date.
Extract the contractor register, offshore service-centre rosters and the IAM entitlement report for access to policy administration, claims, CRM, the data warehouse and document repositories.
Build your own in-scope population from the scoping rule and compare its count to the population the Privacy Office published.
Investigate every individual in your population but not theirs, and treat entitled individuals absent from their population as scoping failures.
testing.done: an independently built population exists with every difference from the published population investigated.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to assignments and completions
actions: Join the independent population to LMS assignments and completion records on worker id and, for contractors, on the access account identifier.
Compute completion against the 98% threshold and against the 100% sub-thresholds for special-category, financial crime and bulk-export roles.
List individuals with data access and no assignment, assignments never completed and completions recorded after the 30 November deadline.
Check no completion is recorded against a worker terminated before the completion date.
testing.done: an independently computed completion rate exists by threshold group with unassigned and post-deadline completions listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, risk-weighted sample of learners
actions: Take 100% of individuals in the 100%-threshold groups who did not complete, 100% of approved deferrals and 100% of access suspensions applied.
Take 40 learners by seeded random selection stratified across entity, location, function and joiner-versus-established status, including at least five contractors and five offshore staff.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Include at least five movers into data-handling roles during the cycle.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, stratified across entity, location and worker type, and covers deferrals, suspensions and movers.

testing.step: Trace sampled completions to LMS records and certificates
actions: For each sampled learner open the LMS transcript and read course version, assessment score, attempt count and completion timestamp.
Confirm the score met the 80% pass mark and that attempts beyond the third were escalated to the manager as the procedure requires.
Confirm the modules completed match the modules the assignment rules required for that job profile and entitlement group.
Treat a completion with no assessment score, or an administrator-marked completion, as unevidenced unless an approved exemption exists.
testing.done: each sampled completion is traced to a versioned transcript with a passing score and the correct module set.

testing.step: Review the course content against the year's real risks
actions: Read the core and role modules in the version delivered and check they cover lawful basis in insurance context, special-category handling, DSR recognition, secure third-party sharing and same-hour incident reporting.
Confirm the ICP 22 component covers group AML/CFT record-keeping and customer due diligence expectations applying to branches and subsidiaries.
Compare the content change log to the year's incidents, DSR failures and audit findings and flag any recurring failure the curriculum ignored.
Sample 10 assessment questions and confirm they test judgement in a scenario rather than definition recall.
testing.done: content is verified against the year's actual failures and the assessment is confirmed as scenario-based rather than recall-based.

testing.step: Recompute joiner and mover timeliness
actions: For every joiner in the cycle recompute completion date minus start date and test against the 30-day rule, using the access-grant date for contractors.
For every sampled mover recompute completion date minus transfer effective date against the same 30-day rule.
Cross-check the IAM grant date against the assignment date to find anyone who held access before an assignment existed.
Report the 30-day joiner completion percentage against the 100% threshold and the maximum days taken.
testing.done: joiner and mover timeliness is recomputed from HR and IAM dates with the access-before-assignment gap quantified.

testing.step: Test the offshore and contractor evidence
actions: Request from each offshore centre and outsourced provider the named-individual completion list for the cycle and reconcile it to their headcount on the insurer's systems.
Compare the content they delivered to the insurer's core module and confirm the assessment and pass mark were equivalent.
Sample five named individuals per provider and obtain their certificate or transcript entry.
Treat an aggregate percentage with no named individuals as unevidenced and raise it as a contract obligation failure.
testing.done: each provider's named-individual evidence reconciles to headcount with equivalent content and sampled certificates obtained.

testing.step: Test deferrals, exemptions and the escalation ladder
actions: For each sampled deferral confirm a documented reason, an owner, a return date and that the individual completed on return or remains within the deferral window.
Confirm every exemption carries an approval and that the exempt individual genuinely holds no personal data access, by checking the IAM entitlement report.
Trace the escalation ladder for sampled non-completers: weekly manager lists, 1 December functional head escalation, and access suspension at deadline plus 15 days.
Confirm applied suspensions actually removed the entitlement in the IAM platform on the recorded date.
testing.done: every deferral, exemption and escalation step is evidenced, with suspensions confirmed as actually executed in IAM.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the individual count, entity, function and the data access held by the non-compliant population.

Assign a root cause — population scoping missed an entitlement group, assignment rule wrong for the job profile, joiner trigger failed, contractor outside the LMS, manager escalation not run — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where individuals with special-category or bulk-export access did not complete, require completion or access suspension within 10 business days.
Feed content-level causes into the next curriculum refresh and rule-level causes into the LMS assignment configuration.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, an access decision for high-risk roles and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the annual training test
actions: Compare the independently computed completion rates to the 98% and 100% thresholds and the joiner rate to its 100% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against ICP 22 Standards 22.3 and 22.6 and ICP 8.1, citing workpaper references and the behaviour measures.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither authored the curriculum nor ran the campaign, sign the workpaper.

Report the conclusion, threshold misses and unresolved access exposures to the Board Risk Committee, copy the AML/CFT component to the group financial crime report, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated ICP-referenced conclusion, completion rates against thresholds and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
